title: Extremely low-end litter pan and not one I would buy; I would consider this almost disposable
text:
I am very disappointed in this litter pan because it is so low end. It works as a litter pan (see third picture with one of my cats in it); but it is not durable and lacks the basic features I expect of a good litter pan.

DISLIKES

- The plastic is super thin.

- The hole (see first picture) is just a cutout and there is no front lip on the pan.

- The handle is cut into the plastic and is very flimsy and easily breakable.

- The litter pan's locking mechanism consists of one tiny nipple in the center of each side, so all it does is hold the cover on. I cannot carry the pan with any litter in it. Also, the nipple is easily breakable.

- The pan's top and bottom seal are not overlapping. This means if one has a cat that urinates all over the sides of the litter pan, the urine will easily seep out onto the walls, furniture, etc.

I personally would not pay more than $6 for this pan in its current state. It works but it is not durable. I am partial to the [[ASIN:B003RQVGKC Catit Jumbo Litter Pans]] and others of similar quality.

The second and third photos show this litter pan next to the usual one I use for my cats.

title: High powered and fairly quiet, saves time
text: This is my second Oster battery powered professional clipper and I like this one even more than the previous model. The battery and charging station are small,  all parts are black with the on/off switch and battery base being a royal blue. It didn't take to long to achieve a full charge,  so aftee an initial oiling, I proceeded to perform a puppy cut on a Shih Tzu who liked this one immediately because it is fairly quiet.  Yes,  the blades heat as it is used,  but the clipping is so clean and smooth that the grooming seemed to be quicker. A chill charge lays a couple of goods,  so you can purchase a second one and have it in the charger while you are using one in the clipper. The design of this is well balanced and easy to maneuver in any position.  The on/off switch is a little stiff but this is a new unit and I do like the large size of Oster switches. title: Razer Basilisk X Hyperspeed Wireless Mouse
text:
[[VIDEOID:4c2e9d2f7b0e6a0691a91cb5e893b6c]] This is a review for the Razer Basilisk X Hyperspeed Wireless Mouse.

For comparison purposes, I also use a Razer Basilisk 16,000 DPI Optical Sensor (wired) and a Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum (wired) on a daily basis. I don’t love the wired Razer, as I’m not a fan of the scroll wheel or the design of buttons 4 and 5.

Right off, I noticed that I liked the scroll wheel on the Razer Basilisk X. It doesn’t have as much resistance as the wired version does. It’s a little clicky and has some resistance, but not so much that I revert to using my laptop’s trackpad, as I do with the wired Basilisk.

The left and right buttons are nice and clicky. The side buttons stick out a bit more on the Basilisk X than on the wired Basilisk, which I prefer.

I have small hands and found the Basilisk X comfortable to use for hours at a time.

Synapse 2 on my Mac could not find this mouse. Synapse 3 on my Windows computer did find the mouse. This mouse is only compatible with Synapse 3. On Windows, I was able to customize the different buttons.

There’s no RGB customization, as the Basilisk X is the less expensive model. I was sad to see the Razer logo doesn’t light up; yes I’m a dork who likes glowing peripherals.

The mouse can be used either wirelessly or with Bluetooth. There’s a switch on the bottom to switch between connectivity types. The Basilisk X uses one AA battery; to help with battery life, I put the switch on BT to keep from accidentally waking the mouse if I don’t have the dongle plugged in. The USB dongle can be stored inside the battery compartment. It’s very small and difficult to remove from a USB port once inserted.

In contrast to other battery powered mice I’ve used in the past, the Basilisk X’s battery compartment is on the top of the mouse. The top pops off so easily I’m worried that it will pop off while I’m using the mouse, especially during an intense moment in a game. All it takes is a little pressure in the right spot, and bam, off the battery lid goes. I really don’t like this.

I don’t have a scale, but there’s a noticeable weight difference between the wired Basilisk and the wireless Basilisk X. The Basilisk X feels very lightweight in the hand. It’s almost a bit too light for me; I notice the difference every time I switch between the mice.

title: Incredibly fun long awaited sequel!
text:
There may be no more complicated series on Earth to try and explain fully to people than the Kingdom Hearts series. I have played and beat almost every game on their various platforms and I still do not understand close to everything. However playing this "third" iteration (there have been far more than 3 releases because of the spin offs) I think you can go in with a fairly simple understanding of what's going on and have a great time. Largely because the story is so convoluted at this point with Organization XIII, Nobodies and The Heartless it can still be enjoyed if you just view the game as my characters are "the good guys" fighting against the bad guys. This iteration more than any other really takes full advantage of the Disney portion of the license placing you deeply inside of incredibly detailed recreations of Toy Story , Frozen, Hercules, Big Hero 6 and Tangled to name just some of the amazing Disney worlds you get to step into. For a Disney fan it is incredible to be able to play in these worlds so vividly recreated. Also if you are a Disney Land/ Disney World fan the special attacks using Disney rides are incredible not to mention those using some classic Disney characters.
My only real complaint in the game is the gummy ship portions which take you out of the action and just feel too simple after traveling to all the amazing worlds but to be fair I have never enjoyed the gummy ship portions.
The game is amazing and truly a love letter to Disney fans. It continues to be the crossover we didn't know we needed and I hope with this game finishing up our story we continue to get more new Kingdom Hearts games in the future as the world still has so much more to explore! Overall the game is truly fun to play and the sequel we have waited a long time for!

title: Great value for a good keyboard
text:
If you are comparing this to a > $200 keyboard, this may not meet your needs but for the price, this is really a great keyboard. It has become the rage to have a volume nob usually at the top right corner of keyboards these days. That is fine, I guess, but I prefer what Royal Kludge has done with this board using the nob as a switch for wired, 2.5GHz and the three bluetooth options. In my opinion, this is much more useful than a volume nob, especially when I can use the F-keys for volume just as easily. Using the nob to switch the keyboard from one device to another is not only easier than using the normal FN key + number key to switch between devices but it will provide a quick visual cue as to what device is currently active.

This is a gasket mounted keyboard. I am not a huge fan of a springy gasket keyboard. This is not such a keyboard. It takes a pretty good press to see any plate flex. What it does do is mute the sound of your keys. That along with the polycarbonate plate makes this keyboard a great option for a work environment where other cube mates may be annoyed by a loud keyboard.

The Sky Cyan switches are super smooth and creamy. They are Royal Kludge's own branded switch and a great option for those who like a linear switch with a great feel. I prefer a top loaded tactical switch so I did replace the installed ones with something of my own choice but I will likely find a good use for these switches. They really are good. One thing to note, they are really tight in the PC plate and will take some effort to remove.

I gave this a 4 star review but for the price and features, it really would be a 4.5 star keyboard and should be one of your top considerations for a keyboard in its price range.

title: We're not mad, just disappointing. Excellent machine & support, app needs more work
text:
It's hard to hate on this drone when it is flying. Mechanically it performs very well in the air. The camera is great & the camera stabilization works very well. The app has been a frustrating experience that has kept me from fully exploring the capabilities of the drone.

After the last app & firmware update we have experienced freezing of the video feed, disconnects from the phone & disconnects from the radio. The good news is that, in the last case, the drone dutifully returned to its starting spot. I didn't have those issues before the update but I did have others.

I have put in a couple of tech requests & their support is very good. In some cases a confirmation email the same or next day & resolution in another day or so. In one case a very nice young man called me to talk me through a gyro calibration.

We have enjoyed using the camera to fly it around the neighborhood. The camera function is fantastic. The attitude adjustment for the camera is intuitive & handy. I'm still learning to fly by the screen so I like being able to "look" up & down to make sure I'm not about to hit something and figure out the location by looking at landmarks & streets.

On the drone platform, the camera can be set to track a person with just the camera & the drone stationary or have the drone follow the person while tracking. We used that to record my daughter's color guard practice. It also has a "point of interest" feature where it flies circles over a particular spot & the operator can start or stop recording while it it is circling. I'm thinking this will be cool for parties this Summer when we can finally have people over again. For now I have is top quality shots of the top of my camper & green pool.

It camera mode it performs very well as a stable, tracking camera. The camera gimble has a lot of range to track a person moving about & the tracking works well. If the person moves out of the frame it will not re-aquire them though in my experience. The camera can be mounted on a tripod or used as a hand-held "camcorder". On a tripod, it kind of hangs off to the side & down so it will interfere with some tripod setups. It is also a bit bulky to use as a camcorder but the stabilization is so good I forgive that. In either configuration a phone has to be used to stop & start recording or take pictures which I do not like & I hope they put out a bluetooth button for that.

The controller is small compared to the ones I used for model airplanes & it is easy to hold. There is no attachment point for a lanyard. The phone is held on a mount that extends out & up & puts the phone in a good place to see but puts a lot of weight up high. The gimbles have a rubber gasket around that makes them water resistant & doesn't interfere with their operation. The controller charges with a mini-usb (ugh) & connects to the phone with included USBC or Lightning cables. The cord going to the phone could be a little more tidy.

The case is nice, thick foam & will hold everything needed to fly except maybe a second battery. It's sturdy enough to put in checked luggage (with the batteries removed of course).

The beginner mode is seriously slow & a good way to get used to flying especially for someone who is learning nose-in hovering & other basics. It also makes a very stable camera platform.

A couple of observations:
I am not great at sorting out things on the app & would prefer robust instructions. I had no idea that the aforementioned gyro calibration was something I could perform myself or that I should have known where to look for it. It took me several tries to figure out how to turn on the tracking features (it has to be "started" after turning it on).

This is my first serious drone so I can't adequately compare it to other models. I used to fly model airplanes & helicopters decades ago & I tend to try to fly these quadrotors like an airplane in line of sight flight. title: Another Love-Hate Relationship
text:
Amazon 1 Star Rating equals to "I Hate It" ... and I do have hatred for aspects of the Bolt, even though I also have love for it.

(Please keep in mind I have owned many different DVR's, such as the Moxi, ReplayTV, and Channel Master DVR+.)

I Hate:

TiVo wants a fee of $600 for a lifetime license, after you pay $300 or $400 for your Bolt. This is insanity! I could understand if they were asking for $600 for the lifetime of the person, no matter what TiVo boxes they swap out in the future.

The design of the box is terrible, in my opinion. I really hate it. (And please do not say they did it only to allow air to escape, because air can escape just fine on their Roamios and on other DVR's such as the Moxi.)

Final thing I hate is the difficulty prying the box apart to swap out the hard drive after the screws are removed. TiVo knows one's hard drive will fail eventually after the warranty, and/or that people will wanna upgrade to a larger capacity drive. They could have easily designed this box with a removable cover just under the drive, instead of making it where you have to take the whole cover off in parts.

Love:

Hands down, the TiVo interface and extra features of the Bolt are superior to any other DVR out there as of this writing. Once you have the opportunity to use Commercial Skip, you'll fall in love. Also, the Quick Mode feature is very nice, and it works well. The speed of the Bolt interface is excellent.

The TiVo software is really easy to use. The Bolt is easy to get set up. I like that if you have to swap out your hard drive, the TiVo software will automatically install itself on the bare new drive.

I like the online and mobile interfaces which allow you to set recordings remotely.

There are countless people online who feel that TiVo's $15 per month (or $150 per year) fee is too expensive ... and of course if you are paying it, you will wish the fee was a more reasonable $10 per month/$100 per year.

I am hoping TiVo has heard the endless complaints of folks who hate the Bolt's box design and who want a flat box. It will be interesting to see if they do a redesign of their next DVR model. And I'm hoping they come out with a TiVo Bolt OTA for cable cutters where the lifetime license fee will be far more reasonably priced than the Bolt's astronomical $600.

title: Beefy, portable power that works with my Pinecil soldering iron
text:
This portable power bank is quite beefy and has some real heft. It weighs 2.5 pounds without the case but with this heft, you get some real power.

It sports two Type-A ports at 18w max, a type-c port at 45W max, and a 110V AC output at 120W max. The type-a ports are fairly standard and isn't anything out of the ordinary. The AC output should be enough to power most laptops but you would still need your laptop's power adapter.

The type-c port was why I wanted this device. It can be used to charge this power pack at 45w, which means you can fully charge this thing fairly quickly (sorry, I haven't timed it). The 45w output of the port allows me to run my pinecil soldering iron at full wattage, which means that my soldering iron can go to 300 degrees within 10 seconds.

Another use I had for this thing was that I had a skunk that was breaking into the crawl space under my house and I needed a camera to keep an eye on the movements of the skunk. Rather than purchasing a motion sensing camera, I was able to take one of my WIFI cameras and power it with this thing. The battery not only lasted the entire night, it only went down by one light (out of 4 lights total).

Two things I wish this power supply had: An adjustable DC output with a barrel connector. This would allow charging of laptops without having to plug in the laptop's adapter. I would also have liked the type-c port to support 100w because many laptops that charge by Type-C require at least 60w output. Those laptops will trickle charge from this power bank but will complain about it being under-powered.

title: Studio-Grade Headphones
text:
The majority of the headphones I use on a regular basis are active noise canceling (ANC) headphones. These come with the advantage of eliminating low-frequency noise so that the listener does not need to crank the volume to hear, but the disadvantage is that the phones twiddle the sound in subtle ways (usually in the bass range to boost volume but they also tend to flatten the highs) such that dedicated audiophiles can really tell the difference. The Munitio PRO40 headphones are my first higher-quality non-ANC headphones. Though I have not had them very long, I already can say I am pleased with them.

These are very lightweight phones and are very well constructed. They are sturdy yet very light relative to their size. Other headphones of their approximate size can get a little heavy over longer periods of time but so far I have not had that problem with these phones. I will say that when I first put them on they were a little tight and they felt a little uncomfortable. It does not take long to adjust to these phones, though, and after only a few minutes I found them to be very comfortable. The pads are soft enough to make wearing for long periods possible.

For headphones in this price range, sound is absolutely the most important consideration. There is no point in spending this kind of money if the sound quality is flat or hollow. These phones have very good sound and are worth their asking price in that regard. The bass is definitely there (and Munitio makes it a point to tout their bass response) and is deep and rich. The midrange is also very strong which is important - many headphones I have used get the highs and lows right but the midrange tends to be flat and lifeless. The highs are bright and clear. Unlike ANC phones, the sound is untouched and is an accurate reproduction from the source. Overall, the sound is very full and rich across the spectrum.

I chose a set of music tracks for testing that I believed would put these phones through a fairly comprehensive listening test, selecting some club tracks, some hard metal, bluegrass and even some choral accapella. As I listened to these tracks, I was startled by just how much more music is there; these phones definitely bring out more detail in the individual tracks, to the point that a few of the tracks sounded like new versions of old favorites. Individual instruments were more distinct to such a degree that I could hear subtle ticks and plucks that I never before heard in these tracks. Music is definitely more spacial as well.

These phones are fine for listening to music through a device like an MP3 player but this is not where they shine most. These are studio-grade phones and are perfect for using with a sound mixing board. I plugged these phones into a mixer used for live recording and was very, very pleased with the sound reaching my ears - what comes through the cans is untouched via internal electronics and is a fairly accurate representation of the sound as it is meant to be heard. Precision is important when recording live and these phones do a great job of reproducing the sound accurately. From here forward, these are the headphones I will used with the sound board.

I cranked up the volume and was unable to get these phones to distort. I did get my ears to ring, though...

I was a little surprised to find that there are no adapters in the package at all - no 1/4" jack and no airplane jack. Considering that the best use of these phones is paired with a mixing board and these almost always require a 1/4" plug, this is an unfortunate omission. An adapter is only a couple of dollars, though, so this is not a big deal in the grand scheme of things.

The storage case for these phones is great - period. It is very crush-resistant, roomy and should provide excellent protection for the phones under normal to heavy use.

These are studio-grade headphones and are far and away better than most headphones I have used. The price is definitely high, but these phones are worth the asking price and will please all but the most critical music lover. For someone working in a studio or with higher-end audio equipment, these are absolutely worth a close look.

title: Fun, but confusing
text:
"Message in a Haunted Mansion" was my second Nancy Drew game (my first was "The Final Scene.") The graphics are beautiful, with numerous little details that really made the Victorian mansion come alive. Nancy is staying with a friend and helping her fix up a Victorian mansion that she is going to turn into a B&B, except strange accidents keep happening that delay the grand opening. Is the house really haunted?
The only problem I encountered was that I must have played out of order, because I kept finding clues and I had no idea what they were related to. The story seemed disjointed and not as in-depth as with "Treasure in the Royal Tower." But I really enjoyed the bandit/Chinese subplot, the séance, and the many puzzles. The sound effects were genuinely creepy: one minute you will be walking down the hallway and the sound of a woman crying comes from nowhere. Or you're walking up a deserted staircase and you hear ghostly whispers.
There are two levels, junior and senior detective. The puzzles are slightly harder for senior detectives, but the plot is the same. If you get stuck you can call your friends Bess and George for hints. I needed to look online for hints quite a bit since, as I said earlier, I must have missed clues since large parts of the story were missing for me.
One of the things that bugged me was the fact that there really weren't many places to explore. You can't leave the house, and you only have access to your room and one other room, the attic, the dining room, parlor, and basement. I was hoping for more rooms/secret passageways to explore. Not having more locations really cut down on the game's length/replayability.
Overall, "Message in a Haunted Mansion" is a fun outing for detectives: a chance to explore a spooky haunted house, gather clues, learn about Chinese art and writing, and dig up clues about a timeless love story and hidden treasure.

I have two cats with more drama than any of my kids has EVER had. One of them is on an intermittent Ghandi style protest fast, and the other one used to eat anything, until learning bad habits from her idol- our grumpy male cat who does not want her around. I was pulling my hair out the other day with no one eating any food repeatedly (including their favorites) when this arrived in the delivery. LEt's see what happened.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
You get two of each type of food. There are blends of chicken and seafood or just plain chicken with egg or chicken itself. The packs are foil packs. They are enough for one meal of the day assuming you are feeding two meals a day.

MOUSSE
This is a mousse style- that means it is less chunks and more creamy, although some flavors have chunks in them.

HOW DID OUR CATS LIKE THIS?
I took one of these packets and split it between the two cats mixing it with the rejected food. Miraculously they both ate! I have used it many times in the last few days to get them to eat the food they are rejecting all of a sudden. It has been a hit when NOTHING was getting our older male cat to eat.

PROBLEMS?
The one thing that is difficult about these is getting the food out. There is a lot left in the packets, but I just fill it with water, fold the top down and shake well. Then I pour this over the food as gravy.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great variety of food that was a shock to me when our cats ate it, this is great to have around the house. At least with the variety pack, you can find out what your cat or cats like and buy that in the future.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This stuff has been a godsend in a very difficult week when I was not in the mood to struggle with cat drama. I am not fond of the packets being hard to get all of the food out of, but the fact that they are eating it is thrilling on its own.

title: Great keyboard, gamery features. UPDATED. My Keyboard is currently a paperweight
text:
UPDATE 2: My keyboard is working again! I received a response from Redragon customer service and they sent me a firmware updater and that did the trick. It took a little fiddling, but I was able to let the updater run while there were random commands from the keyboard being processed. The updater was able to complete and I watched the keyboard restart with it's lighting startup sequence. After closing the windows and programs that were opened by the keyboard, everything seems well again. Thank you Skye from Redragon customer service.

UPDATE: This keyboard no longer works. I've had it for a little over a year. I was having some issues with the lighting not changing. I had it on the default setting and it was getting a bit bright for me, so I wanted to change it to something else. I loaded up the software from the Redragon website. The lighting would not change. I uninstalled the program and rebooted. All was fine except it was still on the stock lighting. I re-downloaded the software and reinstalled. Same thing, I couldn't change the lighting. I noticed there was a firmware updater included with the download. BAD IDEA. UTTERLY TERRIBLE IDEA. I ran the update, now I wish I hadn't. The keyboard now makes random keystrokes while it's plugged in. I cannot control my computer while it's plugged in. I'm quite disappointed in this. I purchased this in November 2019. It's now Feb 2021. So about 15 months and it's a paperweight. I have contacted Redragon Support. They have helped me out in the past, so I hope they will come through again. Like I said in my initial review, they have stood behind their product for me in the past. I had a mouse where the sensor was going bad causing the cursor to be all shaky. They replaced that, no questions asked. We'll see how they handle this one. I will update this when I hear back.

I bought the optical blue switch version. I was having issues with key chatter with my previous keyboard so I wanted to go with optical switches to eliminate chatter ever being an issue again.

This keyboard does the job well. The only issue I had was a non functional space bar when I opened the package. I removed the key and the switch with the included tools. I reseated the switch and it worked after that.

I’m not a fan of the macro keys, but I will live with them. I suppose they are great for hardcore gamers. I Needed the media controls so I was stuck with the macro keys. The backlighting is great. Every standard mode is there and the software is easy to use.

The switches are on the louder side, but not annoying. The tactile feedback is great. They feel more responsive than my old Kailh brown switches, but are louder.

If you are looking for an affordable optical switch keyboard with some gamer features, look no further. Don’t be scared of the brand. Redragon is a great company and they stand behind their product.

title: A refreshing change.
text:
This game is great. It feels like a cross between GTA and Call of Duty with a bit of Splinter Cell for salt.

The game presents a very open world with a plethora of objectives that can be tackled in nearly any order you would like.

Nearly all vehicles are drivable, and each vehicle handles differently. Some climb mountains well, others not so much. And there are plenty of mountains to climb.

The game is beautiful and has amazing long range visuals, such that we would not have thought possible a few years ago. We took a helicopter up several thousand feet and the ground seamlessly faded away as more and more of the surrounding area became visible. Then jumping out and parachuting down was a reverse thrill of the even greater magnitude.

The missions can be done however you like. Run and gun, or snipe and scoot. Some missions will of course be more easily accomplished one way than the other but you are not penalized for using the wrong method.

The weapon and loadout system, including character customization is amazing. So many options, and it is so enjoyable to work through setting your toon up just the way you want.

On the downside, I did not find a significant difference in feel between the various weapons. While this is a little disappointing, I did not find it detracted significantly from the game.

Checkout my game list for other great games.

title: BO3 is an improvement from AW and Ghosts, but still doesn't reach up to MW3 or BO2.
text:
The campaign boasts good acting, and choice. Want to use several selections of customized weapons? You can do that. Want to pursue a different path or method to get to the end of the level, in most cases you can do that. Want to customize your' characters look? You can do that.
No mind-blowing new features or modes, but there are some cool sequences.
There are only a few tie ins to the other BO games story wise and the locations aren't as wide spread as BO2 OR BO, missions are played in sequences in particular locations for the most part, with none of the typical globe jumping from previous games.
Multiplayer continues from the pick 10 system, with a couple interesting new killstreaks, and mobility options. Different specialists add unique perks that can be helpful, but are mostly frustrating when you get owned by someone else.
Zombies has some great characters, but most of the mechanics remain the same.
Visually, BO3 is better than AW and crushes GHOSTS. The story misses a lot of opportunities for tie-ins with the rest of the series and quality character development. Multiplayer lacks the insane rush nature of AW, feeling slower and more deliberate.

title: Great door, works perfectly!
text:
We bought this cat door when we were awakened, two night in a row, by the horrible shrieking and screaming of cats fighting in our living room. We only have one cat, so somehow another cat had gotten through our cat's door into our house. Nothing is so terrifying as the sound of fighting cats waking you up at 3am, so we were eager to get the problem fixed immediately. The Cat Mate door arrived in only a day or two, My husband had to make a bigger hole for it than our old cat door used (we had it installed in a piece of plastic at the bottom of a window), but otherwise it was pretty easy to install.

It took me a few days to figure out if our cat was able to use it. We tried out the key to make sure it opened the cat door (it did), but it seemed like she was always in the house and never outdoors. But after 2-3 days we spotted her outside, so I guess she figured out how to line up the key with the door and time her approach speed. She never has problems now--she goes in and out easily. More importantly, we have had no more nightly visits by the stray cat! Thank goodness. So for us, this cat door has done the job exactly as we had hoped. I highly recommend it if you're trying to keep stray animals out.

title: Great entry level mechanical board.
text:
Coming from a penny pincher background with limited keyboard experience, this board is great! In the past, I always opted for the cheaper, entry level keyboards. Never again!
I don't think I've used a keyboard with such a great tactile feel and satisfying audible feedback since my original IBM AT keyboard. The amount of force required to type is perfectly balanced, for me. I can rest my hands on the keys without accidental strokes. Previous membrane keyboards felt like they required more force to register strokes, so typing on the G610 feels effortless.
The backlighting makes it easier to use in low light setting. Although the board has a button that allows you to change brightness of the backlighting, the default setting is to have the keys light up in a 'wave'. Since the human eye is attracted to motion, I find it very distracting to have a wave of light travel across my keyboard. I wish the default setting was to have a constant backlighting, so this is where my rating falls to 4 stars. I'd prefer to not install more software on my PC, but I was forced to install Logitech's software to control the backlighting.
Another minor complaint is the placement of the caps lock/scroll lock/num lock indicator lights. To make room for media control buttons, the indicator lights were moved to the top middle of the board, where it is not so intuitive to figure out which light is which. There are labels etched under each light, but they are unreadable, even in decent lighting levels.
Overall, I would highly recommend this board to anyone.

title: Excellent Camera
text:
I have been shooting Olympus cameras since 1978. I have always loved the lenses. With over 2,000,000 shots on my Olympus E-500 camera, I decided it was time to invest in a new camera.

I was reluctant at first to try the EM-1 for three reasons:
- The format is Micro-Four Thirds, not Four Thirds. I take 99% of my photos in the telephoto range, and that is what Four Thirds was optimized to use. Micro-Four Thirds is geared more towards wide angle lenses.
- The camera is mirrorless and uses an electronic Viewfinder (EVF).
- I have to use a converter to mount my existing Four Thirds lenses, and converters have a very bad history.

Out of the box:
The first thing that you notice when you pull the body out is that it is SOLID. The thing feels like it is built like a tank. I have not tried the "splashproof" and other claims, but just holding this body I can believe them. The camera fits well in my hand. My hands are a little large, and my pinky occasionally slides off the bottom. I may buy the grip/extra battery holder later if this proves to be a problem. YMMV.

Using Four Thirds lenses:
I have no Micro Four Thirds lenses and a lot invested in Four Thirds lenses, so using them was a key issue. Olympus has 1/17 or 1 MP of the sensor dedicated to phase detection auto focus, the only type of auto focus that will work with these lenses. I find that the system works very well. Focusing is fast and accurate.

Mounting the converter is easy, as expected. Once mounted, you use a button on the side to release the lens. This is a learning issue since I still normally hit the lens release button on the camera body. I anticipate little real problems with this since as soon as I try to put the cover on the back of the lens I realize my error.

Balance with the 12-60 mm Four Thirds lens is excellent. Holding the lens by the zoom collar, the weight is only slightly behind my left hand. I only have to support the body lightly with my right hand. I personally like that balance. Longer lenses like the 70-300 are also well balanced.

EVF:
I have used a mirrored SLR since 1978 and a rangefinder 35 mm camera and 126 film P&S cameras before that. As you might guess, I favor a direct view to see what I am shooting. EVF have issues with resolution and lag when moving to a different point of interest or following a subject, especially in low light.

The EVF has turned out to be great. I really like Olympus' implementation. There is some lag, but it is generally minimal. The "What You See Is What You Get" is a big plus in my book. Adjust the exposure compensation or manual exposure settings, and the view in the EVF changes to reflect what the image will look like. It is not perfect, but it gets 95%+ of what you will actually get. The display of settings is bright, clear, crisp, large, and surprisingly unobtrusive.

The EVF also allows a lot of changes in camera settings to be done without removing the camera from your eye. Use the two dials, and you can see where the focus points that you are using are. Hit the OK button on the back, and you can use the dials to adjust just about every setting while watching the selections you are making in the EVF. Ditto with the other buttons like HDR and auto exposure mode.

HDR:
I had the opportunity to use in-camera HDR while on a recent trip. The day was cloudy, and there was a lot of shadow against bright grey clouds. The in-camera HDR used a series of shots at different exposures and combined them in the camera. The results were better than HDR Pro in Photoshop CS5.5 IMO. I was much, much happier with the dynamic range and overall look of the images. the 10 fps shooting mode was also great for minimizing camera movement, ghosts and other problems associated with HDR.

Image stabilization:
The EM-1 has a five axis image stabilization system for the sensor. That means any lens becomes can be used. The fourth and fifth axes are for rotations. One compensates for the slight turn of the camera that often occurs when you press the shutter button. I had good success using IS in low light with my 70-300 mm lens set at 300 mm.

Scenes:
the EM-1 has many useful scene modes. I used landscape and panorama with great success. The artistic filters and story modes may also interest you. I prefer to do those types of things in post-processing.

ISO:
The camera has an almost insane 25600 maximum ISO. Yes, you get image quality degradation and noise at that ISO, but the in-camera JPEG processor can actually give you some relief from the problems at higher ISOs. I so far have found shooting up to ISO 1600 produces no discerned degradation. I tried ISO 6400 and found minimal issues.

For those who started with film and were in love with the "high ISO" 1000 film for low light shooting, this is a major and welcome advancement. For those newer to photography that have been using higher ISO cameras for a while, the speed may not be much of a gain, but the image quality should be.

The low end ISO is 200, which is the new normal. I do not find it to be a problem. I would rather shoot at a faster shutter speed than have an ISO 100 setting in most cases. There is an ISO LOW setting, but I do not plan to use it. If you regularly shoot in bright light and want lower f-stops, invest in a neutral density filter.

Back display:
The back display is slightly disappointing. It can only tilt up and down, not rotate so that you can see your composition when you are getting into the shot. It works well for shooting over crowds or getting a low angle shot.

On the plus side, the display is clear, bright and a touchscreen that can be used to select a point of interest for focusing and can be used to take the shot in live view mode. You can also use it to select settings to change. The next generation should be even better, and hopefully it will have a screen that rotates.

SD card:
One change from the E-500 that I do not like is the use of SD rather than CF cards. CF cards are nearly indestructible, and a good Sansdisk Extreme card works virtually anywhere, anytime and is virtually impossible to physically break. The xD card slot disappearing is no loss, but not having a second card slot is somewhat surprising given the high-end prosumer/professional positioning of this camera.

Controls and customization:
The controls are pretty well placed for me with the exception of the auto exposure lock button. That is right beside the viewfinder and too far to the left for my liking. You can do a lot of customization with the control buttons and dials, but there are limits. I have not made any changes yet because I am still learning the camera. Overall the defaults seem logical and useful.

This camera has two dials, one on the front and one on the back. The E-500 only had a back dial, so I am learning to use the two dial system. They work well for adjusting and selecting options. I think the second dial was a good addition. Both are conveniently located for my fingers.

Image quality:
All of this is meaningless if the image you get out is bad. The EM-1 does not disappoint. I know that there are people who insist that they need 48 MP or some other ridiculously large number. The reality is that 16 MP is a great size for printing full-size 300 dpi images on your printer or using a commercial photo printing service. If all you do is screen displays, it is about eight times more pixels than you need for a typical 2 MP monitor.

The quality of the EM-1 pixels is very high, and you get excellent out-of-the-camera RAW and JPEG images. I have no problems seeing fine detail at 100% and higher magnifications.

Summary:
This camera is a winner, and it works with my existing Four Thirds lenses so I do not have to invest another $3000+ in lenses to use it. I have a lot to learn, and it will take some time to get the most out of the camera, but out-of-the-box, using my E-500 techniques, it is already doing great work.

title: Razer With Kitty Ears
text:
Speaking as a gamer, Razer makes a solid product. However, this Razer Kraken Kitty RGB Gaming Headset is a bit of a disappointment.

PROS
1) It's a Razer, which means it's *comfortable* and fits well. It's so comfortable, one can wear it for hours and hours on end.
2) It has solid sound quality and *great* THX 7.1 Spatial Surround Sound for Windows 10. (This version is for PC only.)
3) It lights up like fireworks via Chroma.
4) It's pink with Kitty ears for cosplay coolness.
5) It has a retractable mic for streaming.
6) It's wired and connects via USB.
7) Noise cancelling is okay.

CONS
1) The mic is just... Bad. Mine is very high pitched and VERY quiet. The mic itself is either too short or too weak. And as this headset is sold with live streaming in mind, this is a huge issue.
2) If you don't have Windows 10, you don't have full functionality. It's a cute headset with Kitty ears.

Overall, my Razer Kraken Kitty RGB USB Gaming Headset simply didn't perform to spec.

text:
I got this set of headphones to go with our panasonic phone system in your house for our landline. Many times we get power failures so we still keep a landline. But when the power is not out, I like to use our landline for calls. Our system uses bluetooth for headsets so this is where these came in handy.

HOW ARE THESE?
These headphones are red. I love the color. they seem sturdier than expected, There is a slot in the headphones which you can insert a MicroSD card so you don't HAVE to use a player with the headphones (like phone or MP3, etc). These are bluetooth as well and have a volume button.

HOW DO THESE PERFORM?
My family is a bunch of ear phone addicted fanatics. We have some of the best and some of the worst and everything in between. When I started to try these out, I really liked them and was surprised at how loud they were. One of our kids, a daughter, grabbed the headphones to try them and loved them so much, she is getting a pair for her pottery studio to listen to her own music.

ARE THEY TOO LOUD?

ARE THEY COMFORTABLE?
I use these mainly to talk on the phone so I don't have to cradle the phone to my head when working while talking. These are comfortable and as long as I am not SUPER active with these on, they seem to stay on fairly well. They are comfortable and my ears last about a half hour before I want to remove them. Sometimes longer.

CHARGING
These do not take long at all to charge. Within a few hours they were ready to go.

ADJUSTABLE?
These are not hard to adjust and they seem to adapt well to all of our heads.

The sound quality is surprisingly good with these. There is good definition and it is not muffled or out of proportion to the point that you prefer them not to be on. DO THEY BLOCK NOISE?
These do block outside noise well which is another great feature of these.

VOICE?
So far the voice works well with these when I use them on the phone.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a decent set of headphones that are comfortable, block outside noise well, and do well on the phone for both listening and voice as well as music, these are a great choice. I love the red color too.

MY RATING

text:
I've been using the TT685N for years now, and I was excited to upgrade to the V1-N flash. I purchased 2 of them - one for on-camera, and one for off-camera. The on-camera, when shooting relatively slowly, is really fun and it works great. Thing is, for fast photographing, such as with wedding dance floors, intros, speeches, etc, the recycling time is painfully slow. I was shocked at how long the recycle time was, even when using ISO 800, 160 shutter, f/2.2 - this wouldn't require much light from a flash. My SB-700 can shoot 4-5 frames in a row without skipping a beat.

That said, it's a wonderful flash for off-camera, since I mostly shoot at around 1/64 and 1/32 settings in manual - and for that function it recycles fast enough. The reason I'm keeping it for the off-camera is because I don't have to charge AA batteries with this flash, and I really appreciate the magnetic modifiers. And on that note, the modifiers don't seem like quality construction - they were much lighter and cheaper feeling that I expected.

So yeah, give it a go, but be sure it fits your specific needs before committing to it!

title: Far superior to RB guitar
text:
I really like this guitar. For this review I'm comparing it to the Rock Band guitar. (I own a PS3, but have played Xbox as well)

Positives:
- Very sturdy. It's slightly bigger and heavier than RB guitar that makes it feel less like a toy.
- Very responsive--it only takes a slight tip to activate Star Power.
- Unlike RB, the buttons protrude from the neck and are curved, so sliding up and down notes is much easier.
- The buttons are spaced out better than RB, so normal sized hands don't bump adjacent buttons. For new players, it also makes it easier to know where your hand is positioned without having to look.
- It clicks when you strum, making it easier to keep the beat.
- 2 options to activate star power. Tip the guitar up, or hit the button next to the strum bar (works in both games).
- Neck Slider. The new neck slider is kinda cool, allowing you to tap on it instead of strumming notes. It can also be used for a different distortion sound, or in certain parts of the song where the notes are chained together. The slider is disabled when playing RB.

Negatives:
- The clicking is very loud and can get annoying, especially to those in the room that are not playing.
- The PS button / directional controller is too close to the whammy and can easily get bumped. If the directional controller is bumped, it thinks you hit a wrong note. If the PS button is bumped, the game gets paused. Once you're used to the guitar, you learn to avoid it.
- There are limited distortion options. (there's no switch like RB) Very minor.
- Children or adults with very small hands may find it a stretch to play the 1st and 5th button at the same time, but you won't need to worry about this until you get to Expert mode.

I have had no problems with timing, connectivity, or notes registering correctly, except when the batteries are almost dead. If you notice these problems, TRY REPLACING YOUR BATTERIES. The only problem I've had is that my neck slider is overly sensitive when I try to play the GHWT connected notes. Easy solution--I play the notes normally.

title: FIFA has a different feel this year
text:
Finally the champions league is in FIFA! I think this has to be my favorite addition because while you could previously play in cup tournaments or create your own tournament hearing the theme and seeing champions league in a FIFA game just feels different and long overdue.
Now onto the gameplay and this year FIFA feels intentionally slower. There have been some
New mechanics added to the game and
Thus far I am not a big fan of the 50/50 system as it seems random as opposed to skill or rating based. I would say the user loses the vast majority of the battles no matter what player you are using in my playtime so far. Speaking of which the attributes too often feel useless. If I play a through ball to an attacker making a run with a higher sprint rating in open space and they are beyond the much slower defender then the defender should not catch them as often as they do. I understand that they slowed down the whole game for the sake of "reality" however a fundamental element of the game (real and video) is making intelligent runs that expose the defense with a well timed pass. This year feels slower and I am sure those who are excellent with some of the newer trick pass animations and shots will excel but overall it makes the game feel a bit less fluid to me. I like the addition of more physicality in the game but I don't believe the balance is quite right. I also think the change in the passing mechanics so that they are less accurate is a huge mistake as far too often and randomly simple passes like through balls to open teammates or switches to the opposite side of the pitch go awry even when you are using the best passers in the game. It's still a video game and I expect precision not to mention if you watch most of the major leagues around the world the amount of basic passes that go awry without defensive intervention is minimal. I do like the new active touch system which is fun especially on volleys but it will take some more time to truly master.
The graphics from the players to the stadiums and the pitch continue to look great. The commentary also is strong with the addition of Lee Dixon and Derek Rae for the Champions league matches.
The journey mode which I enjoy is supposed to represent the end of our time with Alex Hunter. I have not finished it yet but am enjoying the use of the champions league as a focus this year. I also like the ability to play as Kim and Danny a bit more this year. I do wish there were more consequences to choices you make and branching paths that change your story but hopefully this will happen in future iterations as it would also give the mode more replay value if they hade more endings (like the surprisingly fun multi ending game Late Shift). Hopefully I can update this review once I finish the journey.

Ultimate team is the cash cow so as usual it has a ton in it and can be addictive but the best method for advancing still feels like buying as many packs as humanly possible which admittedly makes it less appealing.

I am enjoying the game despite some of its flaws but right now I would probably say it's maybe 7.5 /10.

This has literally at just three months has doubled the average lifespan of my USB cables. This device which is plugged in 24/7 (unless I need to charge my eReader) gets used numerous times a day, it just doesn't sit there. I'm extremely happy with the durability of this cable.

Update August 10th 2017 - I am amazed. No other cable has ever lasted as long as this Anker. I've had cables fail the same day, the same week and as I've mentioned it has developed a distinct bend from the way it hangs from my tablet, kept in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed, the cable shows almost imperceptible whitening just above the connector from strain but no cracks, splits or crumbling. title: FROM TALIEN'S ZOMBIE SURVIVAL GUIDE JOURNAL
text:
DAY -35: Just saw an ad for Dead Rising. So jazzed! The main character kills shambling zombies in a mall with baseball bats, an umbrella, and a chainsaw. Chainsawing zombie goodness, baby! WOOHOO!

DAY 0: Just got the game. YES! Popped it in and started playing. The main character reminds me of Andrew Dice Clay from The Adventures of Ford Fairlane, only sized like a linebacker.

DAY 1: What the...the text is so small! I can't read anything!

DAY 2: Oh for the love of...Dead Rising is for HD televisions only. I can't read what Otis keeps calling me about, so I can't play the game. Sigh.

DAY 32: My brother was over for dinner and when he looked at my flat screen television in the basement, he pointed out that it's actually a high def television. Yes, I'm an idiot. Back to Dead Rising!

DAY 33: Woohoo, this rocks! So many zombies to kill! And not just zombies; the game is full of psychopaths too. I killed a clown with chainsaws, some big fat cop who looks like Kathy Kinney (from The Drew Carey Show), a pyromaniac who looks like Weird Al, and a weird raincoat/green mask-wearing cult that totally freaks me out. I'm a little behind on the main missions but the game hasn't ended yet so I figure I'm good.

DAY 34: I hate this game so much. I spent hours playing it and when I got back to the security office, the game ended and said I had missed a deadline. Information that would have been useful YESTERDAY! Maybe I'll sell it.

DAY 37: Okay, back on track. It's really upsetting that I don't have time to save all the survivors. So I of course only save the hot chicks. And this one old lady because I love my grandma (God rest her soul). A couple of times I accidentally killed one of the survivors with a sledgehammer when I was trying to kill a zombie. Mental note: people and sledgehammers don't mix.

DAY 38: OH. MY. GOD. The game just crashes at random times. It says the disc is dirty. Only the disc isn't dirty. My theory is that the game uses a huge amount of processor speed, and since I have a refurbished 360, they dialed back the processing power so the Xbox doesn't overheat anymore. Which means Dead Rising crashes it every few times. I am so selling this game, screw this!

DAY 40: It seems like there's some sort of plot to produce cattle...that led to creating zombies in a little town outside the U.S. The main psychopath decided to reveal the U.S. government's illegal experiments by unleashing the zombie plague at a mall to make a statement. It doesn't really make too much sense. Worse, there are multiple endings and I missed the chopper pick-up time on the roof of the mall. I'm going to start over from my last save point (which is few and far between). I'm starting to really hate this game.

DAY 42: I did it! Almost. Now the U.S. military is "cleaning up" the operation by killing everyone. Gee, glad I went through all the trouble to save all the hot chicks. Oh well, a few katana slices takes care of them nicely. But then there's this long battle with a tank and then some military guy who is impossible to beat. I think I'll just sell this game.

DAY 43: My wife said, "After all this complaining about the game, you BETTER finish it." So okay, I'm gonna finish it.

DAY 44: I did it! I beat the main bad guy by spinning around like a top, backslapping the bad guy with what has to be the stupidest move in gaming combat history. But I beat Dead Rising! Take that, only-one-save slot! Take that, crashing-all-the-time processor! Take that, stupid forced story-timeline! I did it! I did it! Did I mention I love this game?

I'll sell it tomorrow.

title: A Healthy Treat Your Fubabies Will Love!
text: I love salmon and have a small piece along with a small salad a few times a week for lunch.  I have a dog and 2 cats who also love salmon  and believe me, they're all over me when I have salmon for lunch. Now, I can eat and enjoy my lunch in peace thanks to Whole Life's Freeze Dried Salmon Fillet!  The pouch includes 6 ACTUAL pieces of real salmon fillet that has been freeze dried and vacuum sealed.  Each piece is hard-I did attempt to crumble some on top of the cat's food but it was just too hard. So now I break a piece off and dunk it in water for a bit to soften it up and that REALLY helps. I"m then able to easily break it into small pieces and put some on top of the cat's dry food as a treat.  And this couldn't have come at a better time.  One of our cats, appropriately named Miss Piggy, needs to lose 2-3lbs per the vet.  She and our other cat Squeaky are now eating dry cat food the vet recommended to help with Piggy's weight loss goal. Naturally, they both HATE the new cat food. lol.  But when I sprinkle it with some Whole Life salmon fillet pieces, they go bonkers and devour the new cat food.  Naturally, our dog Mac sees this and wants some as well so I must also moisten a piece of the salmon fillet and put it on top of his dog food.  (Can you tell our furbabies are spoiled? lol) I've timed it so when i give the animals their Whole Life salmon, I take MY salmon and salad and go into another room, close the door and eat in peace without the animals begging me to share my lunch!  The fillets actually came in handy a few days ago...I had to give Mac 1/2 Benadryl pill but I hadn't been to the grocery store -we were out of peanut butter which where I usually hide a pill when he needs to take one. So I pushed the pill into a piece of Whole Life salmon fillet and Mac gobbled it down, never knowing he had just taken a pill. lol.  I love to spoil my furbabies.  They absolutely LOVE Whole Life's salmon fillets and I love giving it to them because it makes them happy AND because its healthy for them.  My one 'beef' with these fillets is that all 6 are vacuum sealed together.  While its not the end of the world, I do wish each fillet was individually sealed.  There is a bit of a scent to these fillets-reminds me of goldfish flakes I used to feed my pet goldfish when I was a kid. lol.  Again, not a huge issue and I only notice it when I get the salmon out to put in water.  I DO believe the price for this item is fair.  Its REAL salmon.  Its incredibly healthy for my pets and they LOVE it. And, I give it to them as a treat, not an entire meal.  This bag will last us for quite some time , so for me, the price is understandable /acceptable.  I do recommend this product if you own cat(s) and even dog(s).  Makes for a great treat, a food to hid medicine in, purrfect (sorry, couldn't resist!) for finicky pets!

title: Good features and powered by mains.
text:
While solar-powered cameras are convenient, I've found that they have too many compromises when it comes to functionality. In order to save on battery power, the software usually shuts down the camera when there is no activity. Usually, that means nothing gets recorded until the motion detector is set off. In addition, a couple of my solar cameras actually had firmware updates that made them almost unusable because the app can no longer wake the cameras up. This means that the only time I'm actually able to view the cameras are when there is actually motion to set it off.

This Reolink camera doesn't have those problems. It can be powered by a power adapter or power over ethernet. While this makes installing the camera more troublesome, it is worth it because I don't have problems like what I mentioned above.

In addition to solving this basic issue for me, I found that the Reolink camera is much more well-built than the solar cameras that I had previously. The camera mount is made of metal and the camera swivel mechanism is made of high-quality plastic.

The camera is pretty annoying during setup because it has a loud speaker that talks and talks until you finally pair it with your phone app but once done, the app runs like any other app that you might have used. It has controls for the pan, tilt, and zoom functions and it will show both of the built in cameras simultaneously.

Pop in a memory card and you have local recording capabilities with a nice timeline to control playback.

This is a high-quality camera that justifies its price.

text:
I looked at a lot of cases before selecting this one, and I am sad to say I am very disappointed in this purchase. I have an Omoton case for my Kindle PaperWhite. I really like the design of the shell--the way Kindle fits into on it, so I was trying to find something similar, where the entire unit is enclosed all the way around. This was the only case I found which appeared to fit this way, so I ordered it. Build quality is fine, and the Kindle does fit snugly in the case, providing the fit I was looking for. Unfortunately, there is a serious (and odd) design flaw in this case: a small lip that protrudes outwards and runs all the way around the edge of the unit.

This lip serves no purpose, and I do not understand why it was built into the design. I don't know why the lip did not register as a potential problem when I was making the decision to buy the unit--I suppose I thought it would be too small to matter. I was wrong. It matters. It is not an issue when you are not holding it: for example, using the tablet to watch movies and it is supported by the folded case on a flat surface (although this feels somewhat precarious/barely balanced). The issue is when you are holding the case in your hand and trying to read with your Kindle: the lip digs into your palm or fingers and after a few minutes becomes uncomfortable. You end up shifting the kindle to your other hand every couple of minutes. This is uncool, and makes what would otherwise be a great case almost unusable as a hand-held device. I thought about returning it, but given the hassle involved, I decided not to bother for a $12 unit.

I cannot recommend this case. If you plan on reading with this case (i,.e. holding it in your hand for any length of time), it will be uncomfortable (sure is for me anyway).

title: This may be the single player Jedi game we have all been looking for!!!!
text:
The game is surprisingly good and while I had optimism as a fan of Respawns Titanfall series combined with the underrated great single player campaign they delivered in Titanfall 2, EA has unfortunately been EA while on a bad run lately. There have also been issues with both Battlefront games so while the gameplay looked interesting in footage that was shown I feared a bait and switch. Luckily this is not the case as you feel like a powerful Jedi who escaped Order 66 and without spoiling too much of the plot seek redemption from your own guilt. The graphics are beautiful (although some NPC characters clearly have less detail) and with this being the last big name multiplayer title release for the year it ends 2019 on a high note.
The game is so much fun because it truly has the best light saber feel I have felt in any Star Wars game so far. I do wish there were some more force powers but honestly not too many makes the most sense within the context of the story and they are used well. The combat is great too and feels very satisfying especially when you execute some instant kill animations. A possibly helpful recommendation that helped me is take out the ranged attackers first before focusing on others.
The story is pretty good so far and the characters like your mentor Cere Junda and new droid BD-1 are well done. Without spoiling things there are also some cameos of Star Wars characters we know and references to other legendary Star Wars events. It feels like Respawn did a great job of taking elements of other great video game series and incorporating them into the game with their own spin. There is definitely a Souls feel to the combat with an importance placed on timing and blocking. I also love the instant kill reward if you time things correctly with an enemy. In no way would I say this game is as difficult as a Souls game but it has a challenge that can ramp up considerably (however after each “death” the game does not get even more difficult). The enemies do all regenerate on a level if you decide to heal yourself though. There is of course a skill tree as well to develop Cal over time. There are also clear elements of Metroid Prime when you move around the map and an Uncharted/Tomb Raider style adventure feel as you traverse certain areas. You will also definitely revisit previously unreachable areas on planets but it’s fun to go back to areas in planets with more power/skill and the shortcuts you unlock allow for a different path. The game feels very rewarding when you play through and pretty smooth with limited pop ins.
I hope we see more games in this series and that this is a sign of where EA’s future single players games will go. A quality experience not bogged down with microtransactions. I love this game and recommend it highly for any Star Wars or Adventure game fans or for any people who want a more forgiving Souls experience. It is actually hard to put down and I look forward to playing through it again on the highest difficulty.

title: Excellent gaming keyboard
text:
True, this is a gaming keyboard. But if you're looking for a uber-strong keyboard this one will do as well.

This is my first true gaming keyboard as I was always looking for too many bells and whistles. I can say my gameplay is a tad better due the responsive of the keys. There is no question whether you hit the key or not.

The Cherry MX blue keys are made for repetitive strokes. As many as your little fingers can press. Heavy fingered? No problems. Pound away you beast of a human! Each key should be good for 50 million key strokes.

These keys do click and make noise. Most gamers use headsets so this shouldn't be an issue. If your family complains just shut the door or throw them out of your house.

The frame is metal with a decent heft. Less likely to move when fighting Orc's or running tanks against the communists. A nifty sleeve is included so you can bring your keyboard for extended gaming weekends at the Wizard Caves of Uldor.

There's an extra USB port for *charging* only. You will need 2 free USB ports to properly use this keyboard. It would have been nicer for a regular, usable port, instead of charge only.

Included are some red key caps. These are to highlight the WASD and 1234 keys for FPS gaming. The WASD keys are textured which makes it easier to keep your fingers in place during intense battles.

The red LED lights are uber cool and can be customized. Use the FN key and the left/right arrows to switch modes. Personally I prefer a steady glow as I don't look at the keyboard during intense battles.

I've never used Anti-Ghosting or N-key rollover, but here's what HyperX says about it: Game mode disables the Windows key to prevent accidental interruptions, while Anti-Ghosting and full N-key rollover let you press all keys simultaneously, with every keystroke registering and executed as quickly as you command.

FYI: The num lock (1) and cap lock (A) are located on the upper right of the 10-key pad. Lighted too!

All-in-all, I like the keyboard. It's a tad smaller than what I'm used to, but it's designed for gaming and it works wonders. There's a nice audible 'click' when engaging, not the normal 'mushy' feel and confusing. I can type documents as required but can still break away for a rousing Orc battle.

A 2-year warranty is included. Designed in Germany, assembled in China.

title: Oh, my achin' agin' anteriors!!
text:
Santa dropped this off at our house the other day, and I'm pretty sure he had a smile on his ruddy face when he did it. "I'll teach those bleedin' couch potatoes", he said with a laugh. "Ho Ho Ho", and off the old jelly belly flew, with his sleigh full of Wii related accoutrements for sedentary families around the world.

Having the good fortune to have a semi-geek in the house, the Wii thing was soon set up in the kid's bedroom, and after 5 hours I thought I should check on the adult kid and the little kid - just in case.

Santa had sadistically included an extra controller and nunchuk with the package, so added to the pair that comes with the set, a full scale 2 kid war was in progress, covering bragging rights for five included games - boxing (little kid leading), bowling (big kid ahead), baseball (no clear advantage - but then we don't play baseball here, because it's just not cricket), tennis (neither will see Wimbledon) and golf (Tiger's safe for now)

They had set up a Mii (avatar) for each member of the family (self included), and looking at the body shape they chose for me, I immediately remembered that I should make a New Year resolution to lose weight.

Soon enough a challenge was issued, and hours later I emerged as the household bowling champion, but threatening to sue for physical abuse for my boxing loss. (I think they made it personal)

All these games have an aerobic and physical element, and if you don't get yer lazy azz in gear, nothing much happens. Bowling for instance, requires you to swing the controller like you would a bowling ball (making sure that you secure it around your wrist first so you don't put a hole in your TV), and after hours of unaccustomed exercise, your muscles can really feel the burn. And it's not only your arm muscles. One does not bowl without the correct body language after all.

Oh the pain!!

Now they're looking at all the other doo-dads and wing-dings to further their Wii experience, and making strong birthday and father's day hints. IMHO they should drop off their requests to the fat man in the red suit, and get HIM to come over and play some games.

Off to review some Icy Hot and Radian B, and make a massage appointment.

Amanda Richards, December 28, 2008

title: Stable and Versatile
text:
I selected this clamp for working with my mirrorless camera. There are times when clamping to a surface or a pole is more practical than setting up a tripod or monopod, so this kind of solution is useful in those cases. It's a decent clamp system and it works well, though it does require some messing with it to get used to it if you've only worked with a tripod in the past.

This idea is simple here. This is a clamp system that includes a couple of adapters for attaching cameras and accessories so that the camera can be held steady without having to set up a big, bulky tripod or having to hold the camera by hand. It comes with two clamps that can be connected via the ball joint adapter so that the system can convert to an anchor support for a pole as well (not the intended use, but practical nonetheless).

Included in the kit is a 1/4" adapter that connects to a standard camera mount (like my mirrorless), and an adapter for connecting a GoPro. It can be used directly with a cell phone, but it is not ideal for that and does require being creative with the clamps (not recommended); better is using the clamp to hold a selfie stick which in turn holds the camera.

The clamps hold tight as do the ball joints. It takes a little bit of fiddling but getting this set up exactly as desired is possible so that you can get the perfect angle. Further, the system can hold a little weight and has no trouble at all holding my mirrorless camera steady.

It seems to be made well and so far I have not had any issues with loose screws, stripped components, wobbly connectors (when properly tightened) or slipping grips. It's still early on in working with this system but so far I see no red flags.

I am happy with this clamp set-up and I will get some good use out of it. It's a practical solution when a tripod or other mount is not workable. It's not particularly expensive, either.

title: Fantastic Reprise of a Classic
text:
Shogun: Total War was the title that marked the beginning of the Total War series of games -- games which feature a combination of strategic/turn-based play on a campaign map and tactical/real-time army combat on a 3D battlefield map. The original Shogun was a fabulous game, and, after years and several other iterations of Total War, including Medieval, Rome, Empire and Napoleon, Creative Assembly have returned to reprise their classic game, and done so fabulously well.

Shogun 2 drips with the atmosphere of medieval Japanese clan warfare and intrigue. The voices, the music, the scenery, and even the diplomacy are all period and region perfect, and give the game an unforgettable atmosphere. The campaign map reprises the clans of the classic game, with Japan divided among numerous warring clans, each headed by a Daimyo/warlord. The player controls one such clan, and must manage his clan's economy, trade routes and income, family relationships, general loyalties and roles, diplomacy with other clans, construction of buildings, military units and naval ships, spying/subterfuge/assasination/religious conversion and, of course, warfare. The basic outlines are, of course similar to those of the other games of the series, but with markedly less "bloat" than we have seen in some of the more recent titles -- units are more streamlined, which makes some aspects of the battles more intuitive.

The game, however, is set at a challenging level. Even advanced Total War players will find the challenging settings to be very challenging indeed. Newcomers to the series may find even the easy setting to be challenging as well. The AI in Shogun 2 is smarter, more adaptive, and more aggressive, at lower difficulty settings, than in previous titles of the series. This added level of challenge gives the game more depth, and keeps the player on his toes, although it can be admittedly frustrating if you have a low frustration tolerance or are more tuned to the difficulty settings of earlier games in the series. However, if you enjoy a bit more of a challenge, you'll find Shogun 2 to be a wonderfully engaging strategy game that will provide interesting play for quite some time.

In all, this is a must for any fan of the Total War series, and probably the best game of the series to date. Any serious strategy game fan should give this game a shot -- you won't be disappointed.

title: A fantastic system
text:
I have so many great things to say about this system, and very few negatives. Nintendo has done a fantastic job updating the 3DS line and correcting some of the previous problems that older versions had.

The biggest to me is the eye tracking with the 3D feature. My husband has an older and smaller 3DS and the 3D feature doesn’t work as well. It’s a strain on the eyes after a while because it doesn’t stay in focus correctly. With the New 3DS I don’t have that problem at all and can play games for hours in 3D mode without issue. It will go out of focus when I move and shift around, but the infrared kicks on and adjusts it quickly.
Another one of my favorite changes, albeit small, is the slight re-positioning of the buttons downward. It’s not a lot, but it’s enough that the console feels more comfortable in my hands for longer play sessions.

My biggest gripe with this system is how quickly the battery drains in sleep mode. Ideally you’ll want to leave it in sleep mode when you’re not using it so that you can Streetpass with it, but mine only lasts 2-3 days in sleep mode before it needs a charge. It’s not a huge problem by any means, but it’s a little frustrating to take it out of my backpack and find it dead.

Another minor complaint is how small the SD card is that it ships with. Save yourself the headache and just buy a larger card with the system and immediately upgrade it. There’s nothing more frustrating than wanting to download that big beautiful new game and finding that you can’t because your SD card is full.

Overall though this system is great. It has lots of options for games to suit all tastes, a good and steady 3D display, good play-time battery life and a bunch of fun quirky features (like augmented reality) to bring out the childlike wonder in anyone.

title: Our Cat LOVES This  She Is Not Too Sure Of The Fan Yet But..
text:
WARNING: This is an in depth review to help with making an informed buying decision. If you prefer a brief summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE
-----------------------------------------
We had a cat who was so independent I never would have thought to buy something like this for him. Then we rescued a little kitty from a difficult living situation, and she is the antithesis of our other cat who has now passed. She LOVES to be on top of us and whatever we are doing. Let's take a look at this carrier.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This carrier is really cool. It has a GREAT BIG WINDOW in it which is better than the last one we had used for her. It has side vents, and rubberized mesh at the back edges. There are vents on the bottom and top of window area too.

CAN KITTY LOOK AROUND?
The side windows and front window give a perfect chance for the cat to look around anywhere she wants to see.

FLOOR
Our last carrier had a floor mat in it, but this one is flat on the bottom and seems very sturdy and comfortable.

HANDLE
The top handle is padded and easy to carry if you need to.

SHOULDER STRAPS
The shoulder straps on this are padded and curved, and is comfortable to wear.

BASE
The base stands up on its own. This is VERY handy in that we unzip the backpack and the back drops down like a platform she can go up to get into the carrier.

REFLECTIVE
There is a band of reflective tape on the shoulder straps for reflection.

FAN
There is a place for the power bank to put in so the fan will connect, but at this point, our cat loves the carrier, but she is not too sure on the fan movement of air yet. I am slowly getting her used to it.

SO DOES THE CAT ACTUALLY LIKE THIS?
I have to tell you, we have only had the cat in this a few times and this morning, we opened the back and left it on the ground. She ran right over, sat in place and waited to be zipped in. After only being worn for about 15 minutes, we had to put her down as we were doing something she could not be on our backs for. When we opened the zipper, she refused to get out at first. She wanted to stay!

THE BOTTOM LINE
This backpack is a fantastic gizmo if you have a cat that loves to be with you but is underfoot all of the time. It helps keep them close to you while allowing you to do what you need to do without tripping on him/her. This backpack is a thrill for our cat. She loves it and gets in it willingly. The only time she does not like it is when she is outside in it as she is an indoor/outdoor cat and loves to do her own thing when outside.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is fabulous. I am SO GLAD to have it. It is solving a problem for us (clingy cat) so that kitty has her together time and then goes out on her own feeling all happy.

I have a car with Android Auto / Apple Car Play and a single USB port to connect to them. I have two cables attached to that one port with this device- one cable goes to my Android phone, the other cable goes to an iPhone cable, and switching between the two is as simple as pressing the button on the unit! No more unplugging one and forgetting the put the other back in before my wife takes the car. Plug in the appropriate phone, and press the button if it doesn't start automatically. I'd imagine this would work well for all kinds of scenarios... if you have a computer with two different input devices (a mouse and trackpad, or 2 keyboards, etc) and want to switch between them without changing the plug as well. title: The more like Mass Effect 2 the better
text:
For over a year now I have awarded the greatest Xbox 360 game of all time to Mass Effect 2. Not only did I love the cinematic approach they took in Mass Effect 2, but I also accounted the leap forward from Mass Effect 1 to Mass Effect 2. The combat from 1 to 2 was updated to be faster paced, more mobility and an over all more polished experience. The conversation system was improved adding more camera angles so each discussion was like a well directed movie. The emotional ties to each character was multiplied as well.

So, in short, I guess what I am getting at is I value the quality of a product AND what improvements have been made.

I HATE paying $60 for a re-hash of the same game. I have no problem with more of the same, but that should be under the title Downloadable content. If there are going to be real improvements then that warrants a full purchase.

That said, right here, right now I want to dethrone Mass Effect 2, holder of Best Xbox 360 RPG game for over a year and hand it to Dragon age 2.

Surprised? You shouldn't be. Download the demo.

The game has had a MASSIVE overhaul! The graphics are now on par with its cousin Mass Effect 2, and the storytelling is far more engaging. Combat is more fluid, and actually fun! The classes are their own! The music is better. The characters more lovable. The list of improvements goes on and on.

Tell me your thoughts after reading my comments and playing it for yourself....
