title: Versatile for users with multiple USB devices
text:
I received this as a review sample and tested the claimed specifications on a few platforms. The following are my observations that, with Debbie Lee Wesselmann's excellent review, should give you a complete picture of this hub.

First, word about using this hub for charging devices. The specs on this product page at the time of this review claim that this hub will NOT charge devices. Actually, it charged my two phones and another device while I was doing other tasks. Perhaps the specs mean it is not intended to be a standalone charger. The only thing that I do NOT like is the wall wart type power supply that is approximately 3x2x2 inches. It can (and does) block adjacent plugs in my surge protector. However, I can live that that considering the functionality I get from this hub.

My favorite feature and the reason I awarded this hub five stars is the integrated electrical safeguards that protect against over voltage, over current, leakage and short circuits. This may not be a big deal for cheap peripherals like mice, but for an expensive hard drive or my Galaxy Note 3 it's a welcome feature.

If you have a computer and peripherals that are USB 3.0 compliant this hub will boost your transfer speeds significantly. For example, my new Samsung Note 3 will transfer at the 5gbps speed, but frankly I do most of my data transfers over WiFi. However, if you wanted to attach an external 3.0 hard drive to your laptop this hum will allow it to operate to it's full potential - which is lightning fast.

Set-up is easy. You literally connect the included power supply, plug it into your system's USB port and switch it on. All of platforms with which I tested it immediately recognized the hub and the things I plugged into it (which included a flash drive, mouse, two snart phones (Galaxy Note II and Note 3), and a speaker that is powered by USB.

This hub works with Windows 98 (I have an old Sony running it and this hub plugged in and worked with it), and above. I know it works with Win XP, Vista and 7 because I also tested the hub on those platforms. I do not have access to a Windows 8 system so am taking the manufacturer's word that it works on that too. If your experience is different please leave a comment.

One final feature that makes this a five star hub in my opinion is the fact that this will simultaneously support maximum data transfer of up to four high speed devices (three of which can be USB 3.0) plugged into it. Of course the host system needs to be USB 3.0 too, but the hub will sling data as fast as the host can accept it. Not all hubs will operate in this mode, and I suspect that the external power supply has something to do with that level of performance.

text:
Security Warning: All devices from Xiongmai, a Chinese OEM who manufactures white-label video surveillance equipment, come with an always-on cloud feature called XMEye P2P cloud. This feature contains serious vulnerabilities that allow attacks on millions of devices, even ones that are behind firewalls.

Millions of security cameras, DVRs, and NVRs contain vulnerabilities that can allow a remote attacker to take over devices with little effort, security researchers have revealed recently.

All vulnerable devices have been manufactured by Hangzhou Xiongmai Technology Co., Ltd. (often referred to as Xiongmai), a Chinese company based in the city of Hangzhou.

End users won't be able to tell that they're using a hackable device because the company doesn't sell any products with its name on them, but ships all equipment as white label products on which other companies put their logo on top. Evtevision is one of said companies.

If the product description mentions anything about "XMEye," then despite the logo on the front of the device, the equipment was made by Xiongmai.

As you can see in the third bulleted point at the top of the listing:

“Easy view on Smartphone via Xmeye, PC tablet via CMS,and Web browser IE.”

This is, without question, a Xiongmai device. Installing it or any of its software would place the privacy and security of you and your family in serious jeopardy.

Most security companies have banned selling these types of cameras for the reasons I have explained.

As soon as I opened this camera and started examining it I recognized some telltale signs and therefore did not set this up on my network. I caution everyone to avoid these products completely.

Cons

title: Doesn't Play Nice With My Fender Telecaster
text:
The setup of this learning "game" is horrible. I know how to play chords, scales, etc and wanted something that would actually teach me real fundamentals, as I've never been to music lessons.

First off, the tuner on this thing is grade-a garbage all the way. I have 3 separate tuners, all spec the same tuning, then I use the Rocksmith Tuner and it's telling me I'm tuned sharp. So you actually want me to learn songs out of tune? Suuuuuure.

Secondly, the calibration feature on this is almost useless. I am using a 60s Telecaster Classic with the volume and tone both cranked, and the calibration is still telling me the signal is too weak. I was finally able to get a "calibration", but had to set my selector switch all the way to the bridge pickup.

I thought I would be good to go at this point, so I started in on a couple of lessons, just as a very quick brush up and to get them "marked off" as being accomplished. Here's where Rocksmith started in on failing me completely. "Let's find the 3rd, 5th and 7th frets.." easy peasy, right? NOT SO FAST. It won't even recognize that I'm playing the 7th fret on low E. "That sounds like the 8th fret. Let's give that another try." REALLY?

So at this point, I feel like this unfinished turd of a learning program is actually going to be detrimental to my learning process. At this point, I'd much rather just get out my old chord books and dive into learning some of my own progressions and crafting my own style. I truly hope that if you've purchased this game, it actually works well for you.

TLDR version: tuner is inaccurate garbage, game doesn't recognize proper notes when played properly.

title: Where's the adventure?!?
text:
I rated this game four stars for fun, but overall three stars based on the fact that it veers so far from the Donkey Kong legacy it does not deserve to have the DK title. Had this been a different character with a different name my disappointment in this game would have been much less--but having a history full of fond memories of the Donkey Kong series I hate to say that this one certainly does not live up to the name. It is very obvious that DK: Jungle Climber was not made by RARE. There is no real adventure incorporated into the game. The concept is new and enticing--Donkey Kong spins on pegs...wooden pegs...stone pegs...iron pegs...ice pegs--they change from level to level. And DK has some interesting new techniques with this game, such as the attack method, and his ability to fly. However, those (and the graphics) are the only perks to the game. The story is average at best. There are very few extras outside the levels, and achieving 100% completion is not worth the time spent. There is a maximum of one bonus barrel in each level (if any at all) and the challenge is always the same--catch bananas in a barrel, whoopee. There are items to collect within the levels, such as the KONG letters, the banana coins, and the DK coin, but they serve no significant purpose other than free men and useless cheats. And don't be fooled by the cover, you cannot play Diddy as you have been able to in past games. If the level manages to actually have a DK barrel, Diddy comes out and sits on DK's back. When DK gets hit, Diddy goes away. My biggest complaint is that I felt that some of the levels were entirely too difficult. Not difficult because of lack of skill, but simply because it would take several times of playing a certain part of the level over and over and over until you figured out the strategy needed to beat it (since DK dies so easily), and by that time you are so tired of the playing the level you're ready to just put the game down for good. I remember spending about 40 men trying to beat one level (and having any more than 20 men is a major feat!)

Overall, I'd have to say if you've been embedded in the DK games of the past, don't expect the same level of activity and fun with this one. If you are new to video games or the DK series, you will probably enjoy this game. But I encourage you to try some of the older Donkey Kong country games, which were developed for SNES but are also available as GBA games and can be played in the DS.

This came with a nice bubble wrap around it in a box with some packing. Amazingly it was not chipped or damaged.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is ceramic. It is fragile, so you have to be careful with it, but it does make a great addition to any tank with plecos, small fish, shrimp, or even small cichlids.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like how this looks and the design is great with many exits which my fish prefer. They don't tend to like houses with only two entrances for some reason.

title: Lots to like, but somewhat flaky
text:
Been using for a few months now. Initially seemed like an excellent upgrade over an inexpensive single wifi router, but I've seen enough issues that I'm not sure I'd buy again. The worst failure was when I switched from Verizon Fios coax to ethernet and tried to use this as my main router. It worked... for about a week. At first, I just had trouble connecting to corp sites, so I thought it might be my corp network. Later that day, I saw issues with personal devices. Connecting to the router web page was super sluggish and the cpu was pegged. The next day, I went back to using the verizon router as the wired backbone and only using this set for wifi---much better. But, I still see occasional flakiness. Yesterday, one of the units wouldn't connect. I brought it closer to the other units---no dice. I rebooted. I connected it to the network via an ethernet cable. Finally, I rebooted the main/router unit and things went back to normal. Every 2-4 weeks one of the units has issues. Sometimes rebooting that unit is enough. Occasionally I have to reboot the main unit. One of the extender units connects via both wifi and powerline. The other extender unit only connects via powerline (it's too far to use wifi). The powerline-only unit is the one that tends to have issues. But, that was the point of buying this system.

So, the system seems good as long as you don't mind doing a ~weekly reboot. I see about 30Mbps over the powerline-only unit---not fast, but generally reliable.

I've started using MoCA (ethernet over coax) and will likely use that as my backbone in the near future---it's faster (I've seen ~300Mbps for a local transfer over MoCA/ethernet/wifi) and seems to be more reliable than this tp-link set over powerline.

Edit: I ditched this in favor of an EdgeRouter X and Ubiquity access points and am happier now. The Deco system was okay, but far from ideal.

title: Not particularly engaging
text:
Takeda is based on the exploits of Takeda Shingen, a real 16th century Daimyo (a man with land capable of producing more than 10,000 koku of rice) who lived in feudal Japan. The country is experiencing violent civil war and Takeda struggles to carve a place for himself and his family in the brutal political climate.

Gameplay consists of a very straightforward combat campaign with the focus on tactical battle strategy. As Takeda, you control swordsmen, spear throwers, archers, cavalry, and riflemen (if you can acquire the firearms technology) and arrange squads into one of several formations, each with specific functions. For instance, attack formations include the tiger and the snake, while defensive formations feature the half-moon and circle. Battle formations include a center, wings, a reserve, and flanking detachments. You can command troops to move around the battlefield and attack, make them walk or ride faster in an all-out attack, regroup, or retreat if the battle is going badly.

Before a battle, you select a formation and place your troops in whatever combination you feel will be most effective for the mission. Typical mission goals involve attacking enemies, cutting down flags, and decimating troops. The terrain changes with each scenario; some are open battlefields and others have the enemy ensconced behind walls. There are no siege weapons, but troops can be commanded to break down doors and enter the enemy's fortress.

In the beginning, gameplay seems deceptively easy, but as the campaign continues, battles rapidly become more difficult and require extra attention to strategy and tactics. Fortunately, battle length is reasonable since you're not required to hunt down every last enemy soldier once objectives are met. Between battles, you can choose various actions: rest troops, make political alliances, manage your military, or, perhaps even marry. These decisions add a bit of role-playing, but are brief and don't appear to have much impact on the game. Resting troops gains strength, but also gives the enemy time to gather their forces against you.

While the designers are to be commended for the game's attention to detail and originality of subject matter, Takeda is not particularly engaging. With very few decisions to make regarding management of troops or resources, gameplay moves along swiftly, but battles eventually become repetitive. If you or an enemy is seriously outnumbered, the outcome is almost a foregone conclusion and strategy becomes largely unimportant. For fans of feudal Japan and realistic strategic combat, the game may be enjoyable, but casual PC gamers may not find much to hold their interest.

We have a cat who in contrast to our last cat is not at all fussy. She eats a lot of different food. I figured this might work out for her. Let's take a look.

HOW IS THIS PACKAGED?
This comes in a two tier box of 24 cans. Each can is a general serving for a larger cat or 2 servings for a cat that eats less. It has a pull off top on it.

HOW DOES THIS SMELL AND LOOK?
Honestly, none of my family members like how this smells. It is not very appetizing.

HOW DOES THE CAT LIKE IT?
Our cat was very excited when we opened the first can, but since then, she won't finish the cans even if we only give her half. She will eat just about any other food, but this one she is just not that fond of. If we put other food in the dish next to it, she will eat that and still pick this out.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Our very hungry non-fussy cat is not fond of this. I am not sure why, but it does not smell or look as nice as other cat foods, so we may just end up gifting this to a cat shelter.

title: A Nice Bag For Your Expensive Investment
text:
If you're lucky enough to have secured a PS5, then you know what an investment it is between the console, controllers, games, peripherals, etc.. So, having a solid way to transport your pricey gear is paramount.

This PS5 carrying case from Connyam is a great way to store & carry your system. The bag quality is on par with a heavy duty nylon laptop bag. And it's very roomy once fully expanded. Plenty of room for your unit.

There is a zipper pocket on the outside of the bag. However, there are no pockets or compartments on the interior. Instead, you are given padded fabric dividers (again, like you would find in a laptop case) that will allow you to construct compartments for your accessories, cables, etc..

There are no images or instructions included with the bag. So be sure to look at the Amazon listing for the intended layout.

I would say this bag is water resistant, but NOT waterproof. So if you had to bring it through the rain, I think you would be OK. But standing with it in the rain, I'm not sure I would want to risk it. There is also a carrying strap as well as a stitched set of handles.

So to wrap up, if you think of this bag as a heavy duty laptop case, but instead for your PS5, then you will have a very good idea of what to expect.

title: Great Value
text:
After retiring my well used and beat up Welt tripod after 35 years of field use and began looking for a new tripod I was shocked when I saw the prices of medium to light weight tripods for 35 mm camera use. $200-$300 -- are you kidding me? I like quality and long term durability (as was my Welt, but...no longer made) and am usually willing to pay for it. However, I decided to give this relatively inexpensive Benro a try and couldn't be happier. I've had it in the field 8 times already, setting it up in water, on muddy slopes, in freezing temperatures and it performs very well for me. The legs extend easily. It is firm. It is light, and with the attachment of a shoulder strap is comfortably carried. I also purchased the Benro BR268 Ball Head for it and it too is of high quality and excellent functionality. This is a great value.

----
Update March 2012. This may be moot, as Benro no longer makes this model. It has been updated to the A0580F as far as I can tell. Anyway, this inexpensive aluminum tripod has performed great in the field. I've done my best to beat it up everywhere from a hike to the bottom of the Grand Canyon to sloughing through the Everglades. It works fine. The Benro Ballhead BR268 is another story. The quick attachment/release spring loaded button/pin now longer works and the entire mechanism has too much play in it. I only paid $38 for it. So I upgraded to a Manfrotto 496RC2 which works wonderfully, smooth and tight. As I was researching ballheads I checked out tripods. Nothing comes close to the value, portability, and toughness of this cheap Benro. There isn't anything out there with the stability and light weight of this Benro. At 2.4 lbs it is lighter than all Carbon Fiber tripods of the same relative size costing $250 and up.

Note to reviewer who complained that Amazon.com should have better details on the size and weight. He is right, but I think most people do the research and find that information elsewhere, then come back to Amazon.com to buy. Benrousa.com is easy to find and has all the data you could want.

title: Easily in my Top 10 games of all time - ...
text:
Easily in my Top 10 games of all time - and I started playing games in the 1980's with Super Mario.

The open world feels big and open without feeling overwhelming, there are some areas that are innately more dangerous than others, usually because of the density of zombies in that particular area. The graphics are good and the developers are staying on top of updates - the released a fix for the patch that stopped the modders from legitimately modifying the game. Good job devs.

Gameplay is fun and enjoyable, I've finished the game and started playing it again. The story is engaging enough to keep playing, so I'm not knocking it. The melee combat is the best I've seen yet, although I'm not overly familiar with melee in games like Skyrim and Assassin's Creed. The parkour aspect of the game is enjoyable as well, it doesn't feel forced but it feels compelling, which is exactly how a feature should be implemented. The disturbing thought of running through the streets decapitating zombies is so weirdly cathartic, but it IS a release and is enjoyable. I haven't hooked my Xbox One controller up to the PC to play it that way, but if it's half as good as the PC controls then it'll be fine.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this game if you're looking for a fun hack and slash game with some deeper elements like decision making (do I go the long route or the densely populated route?) and some hopping from girder to girder. On a scale from Conan O'Brien to those-chainsaw-guns-from-Gears-of-War, I give this game 19 [Bolter's Flesh].

You'll understand once you play it.

title: It works, but its not the best one.
text:
I wish I could give this 3.5 stars. It works, and helps in all the ways I didn't like my old one, so it is worth at least 4 stars. But there are some things about it that could really use improvement.
To explain, I had a nice backup camera that I installed previously which only ended up being about 100 degrees of view. This wasn't as wide as I hoped, and only showed me what was directly behind the car. THIS camera, however, is a full 170 degree wide, which even shows the edges of my bumper in the fisheye effect. I can see the space next to me, cars behind me, everything that I can't see well usually thanks to the cloth convertible rear view window I have. Thankfully they used the same wiring harness as my previous camera so I didn't need to re-run my power and reverse trigger from the rear light, all of that I could keep which made the wiring pretty painless.

But what I didn't like:
1) The camera is VERY noticeable and it sticks out pretty far. I found the license plate holder covered up the state label of my plate and stuck out too far (camera was beyond the frame of my car) so I used the 2nd mount it includes which can attach to the plastic area over my plate. But even that, because of the mounting bracket requiring space above and behind the camera, sticks out like a sore thumb and still sits the camera beyond the bumper. As in, if someone parallel parks and gives my car a "bumper kiss" (as they call it when parking here in NYC), I have no doubt it will damage the camera as it hits there before it touches my bumper. As you can see in the included picture, bumper kisses are common here.
I turned the camera down so it is at least not sticking out past the bumper, but more in line with it now. I still get a good enough view thanks to how wide the camera is, but I wish I could position the camera better with more choice. I'm forced to use it like this or risk damaging the camera.
2) The picture quality is just OK. The older camera I'm replacing may have only been 100 degrees and not wide enough, but the quality of the image was superior. This one looks more like an old cell phone in color reproduction and smoothness. That's ok, it does the job I guess, but the old one was more pleasant to look at, especially at night. This works well enough at night, but my old one spoiled me because I know it could be better.

All in all, its a decent product that honestly gets the job done. But I wish it had better ways to mount it directly to the car in a way that takes up less space / looks sleeker / doesn't protrude, and that the camera image quality was a little bit better, especially in low light. But it'll do the trick if you want a cheap wide angle.

text:
I decided to buy a pair of noise canceling headphones after moving to a different location at work where I am in closer proximity to a rack of computers that runs constantly. After a short while the whirr of the fans in the computers and the rack in which they are mounted gets very tiring and annoys the ears. After doing some research, I finally decided on the Bose QuietComfort 15, and almost immediately I have seen that I made the right choice.

I was fortunate enough to get my hands on one of these before I committed my money so I could test the quality. I was very pleased when I put on the headphones, turned them on and all of the ambient noise around me simply vanished. The sound of the air conditioning, the murmuring of people chatting around me, even traffic outside was reduced to such a degree that I felt like I was in a bubble. I bought them on the spot.

I put these headphones through two major tests outside of work.

First, I plugged them into my iPod and turned them on. All I could hear when the music played was the music. Talking around me was overcome by the noise cancellation and the music, which was not set to a particularly high volume. As many have commented, the bass is very rich with these headphones but that's fine with me, as I really appreciate good bass response. Treble and mid-range are also good, though not quite as bright as the bass.

The really big surprise was when I plugged them into the mixing board where I was doing live recording. I was shocked at how effectively I could hear every sound coming through the microphones but practically nothing else. The sound was clear, crisp and not muddied in any way I could ascertain, which gave me a much better idea of what was recording onto the CD. I had used a lesser headset for this purpose, but no longer.

Some noises do get through, such as loud talking and even the typing on my keyboard, but those sounds are muffled quite a bit. The idea is to eliminate droning, obnoxious noise such as engine noise (there are several mentions in the documentation about wearing these on planes), while still allowing certain things to get through. These are certainly not perfect in that regard but they do come close.

In the past I have bought headphones only from either Sony or Sennheiser, with a very strong bias for the latter. This is my first set of Bose headphones and they are definitely the best pair I have ever used (let alone owned). I regard these as very much worth the price and gladly recommend them for anyone wanting to hear nothing but the music without blasting out the ears. These are high quality earphones and will please the enthusiast looking for good sound as well as the traveler looking for a quiet ride.

title: RPG for PC goes console
text:
I have to agree with a couple of the other reviews that are already up: this game's a disappointment, especially after such a terrific lead-in as "Dragon Age: Origins".

I've been playing RPGs since before the first game in the Ultima series; that was decades ago. RPGs were developed back in the days when consoles didn't exist. They were designed around PCs. One of the main reasons I never switched to Macs was that there was no gaming software developed for them to speak of. If you were a gamer, you played on a PC.

And I have to acknowledge that maybe the younger generation which grew up with Playstations and Xboxes and all that may really like this game. But I'm an old hand and a traditionalist when it comes to gaming.

On the upside, the visuals and graphics in this game are absolutely phenomenal. No question.

But this time around, they've managed to take the "role" out of "role-playing".

Most notably, you no longer get to choose your character's dialogue. That ability alone kills the immersiveness of the game. Previously, as you chose what your character was going to say a real conversation could (or may not) develop, depending on your choices. Instead, we now have a "dialogue wheel" which allows you to choose (generally) one of three tenors for your statement, sincere/conciliatory, joking, or hostile. So, you click on one and then your character speaks whatever he's going to say. I was often very surprised by what popped out of his mouth, and often found myself thinking that I certainly wouldn't have chosen that option if I knew what was actually going to be said.

Obviously, this wheel severely limits the range of conversational options, and the player's actual engagement in what's going on.

Combat is fast. And I mean FAST. There's no longer any real strategy involved. It's pretty much just hack-and-slash. Again, obviously the console approach, not traditional PC RPG. There's no longer any real ability to set up a strategy in your battles as you could in the previous game. In Origins, I was a master at ambushing and luring opponents into traps. Well... that's not really much of an option anymore. Now it's "I see you!", and the furball's on. Boring.

Too bad. After Origins I had high hopes for the re-emergence of the traditional RPG for PCs. Clearly, the developers - at least, in this case, Bio-Ware - have made the decision to design around the console players and turn the game into a button-mashing experience. Naturally, that's their decision to make, and I guess if that's where the money is in their market, maybe I'd do the same thing, too.

But the metaphor that comes to mind is that if you were looking to read a good novel, in this case you'd be buying a comic book.

text:
Crysis 2 like most people have said in the reviews, is a 100% console port, even though Crytek themselves have said that Crysis 2 will predominately focus on PC gamers, what a joke that was. Day one, the game was broken for PC -- serial numbers weren't working or saving. Multiplayer was a joke, the first game I joined, there was already a hacker (no joke). I would go on about this game, but I think other reviewers have summed up this game much more than I can.

Good:
*Singleplayer was fun for sometime, that's pretty much it.
*Sound effects were pretty decent.

Bad:
*Although singleplayer was fun, the story was boring and uninteresting to me.
*Recycled/lack of enemy AI aliens.
*Consolized gameplay to appeal to MW2 players (Multiplayer also has what you would call 'perks' -- yeah, that says it all.)
*Graphics were no where near as great as the original Crysis/Warhead.
*DirectX 9 API was used; I guess Crytek was too lazy to develop it in Dx11, so they want back to 2002 APIs. C'mon, even Crysis was running DirectX 10.
*No manual save(s) -- your progress is saved via-checkpoints, no hitting "F5" or loading from the escape-menu. How is that for a console port?
*Multiplayer as of when this review was written, is hacker infested. Even Crytek is aware of this. I've had more fun playing the original's multiplayer than this game, even though I was never good in Crysis Wars.

Overall: Crysis 2 reeks of console part, right from opening menu, all the way through its unoriginal gameplay. This what happens when developers try way too hard to compete with the Call of Duty series. It has to stop.

text:
I found this game when I was searching for a "viking" type of game for my husband.....who is 6'7, Swedish and usually loves ANYTHING having to do with vikings. I had never heard of this game before .....but I saw some reviews on other sites for this game and was surprised at how highly rated it was. I bought a cartridge and my hubby didn't care for the graphics....as he plays the PSP and Wii and cares for more realistic looking games.

HOWEVER...I decided to play The Lost Vikings myself and let me tell ya....this game is NOT easy!! You are playing as 3 vikings who each have their own talents, and you have to play each level inter-changing them to make it past obstacles. For example : One viking carries a shield. He usually has to walk in front of the other vikings in case of an attack. Another viking carries a sword and a bow. That one usually has to stand BEHIND the one with the shield and shoot the attackers. The third viking is the only one with the ability to jump...and also to knock down walls. He usually picks up the keys and extra health foods if they are on higher shelves that the others cannot get to. I'll admit, I bought this game used (without the directions) so it took me a while to figure out the controls. The frustrating thing about this game (for ME anyway) is that you need ALL 3 vikings alive to pass to the next level. If even 1 dies....you may as well quit the level and start it over again. title: A review from an actual Fallout fangirl
text:
No reason to hate this game, not sure how people could buy this game without knowing it was online only. There was enough press for months and a huge launch at a gaming convention saying just that, "ONLINE GAMEPLAY ONLY." That's a not a reason to give it a one star review. That said, the game is freaking fantastic. One of my favorite things to do is wander the wasteland, build camps, and scrap, scrap, scrap.

Everything you love about the previous Fallout's is here. You start as level 1, you gather supplies, you learn how to make/modify armor, guns, ammo, water, food, etc. You will fight ghouls, mutants, scorchers, rad scorpions, radiated animals, and the like. Sure, there's no NPC's, but you will spend your time trying to figure out what happened to them through holo tapes. There are mini missions that help you rank up and earn perk points as well as stimpaks and water. Similar to Red Dead 2, you need to make food and purify water to stay alive, this is a pretty easy task.

In just a few hours of gameplay I ranked up from a level 1 to a level 7 by completing challenges, I built myself a little camp house by the river with a bed and made a crafting station for armor and cooking, even set up some turrets. You can store all your scrap in a vault-tech trunk at your camp AND anywhere you see a blue vault-tech trunk (in town or at a vendor) all your stuff is there! No more running back home to store all your junk. You just store it on the go. Then if you want move north or where-ever, you just pick up your entire camp "as is" and take it with you. No need to start all over again!

So...combat. Its numerous. Can be difficult at times until you get the hang of it. Even though I had a pipe gun very early on, I found it easier to use an axe, pitchfork, and hatchet. I died often when I first started but now I just run into combat with my fiery pitchfork and take out enemies with one hit. I feel like this game is similar to playing Fallout 4 in survival mode.

Other players: they are awesome, they are helpful, they are polite. We are all working toward the same goal. There are no griefers. As a level 3, I ran into another player who was ranked in the 100s, he was fantastic. We miked up and he gave me lots of tips, helped me out on a couple missions, made me a weapon and said that it was more fun for him to help out the lower ranked players and guide them through the game. Seriously! There is hope for humanity after all!

title: Better than I Expected; Doesn't Lose Power Like Canned Dusters Do
text:
I use canned dusters for a variety of purposes, from cleaning keyboards to cleaning up my electric shaver. These sometimes leave residue behind, so I was interested in trying this electric duster to see if it would cut down on residue and save money in the long run. I will confess that I was not very optimistic and thought it would be underpowered. However, it has proven to be as effective as a canned duster in cleaning keyboards and other equipment, without leaving any residue and without losing power like canned dusters tend to do as they get cold.

This device is smaller than a tea kettle and relatively light. It requires an AC outlet so it does need to be plugged in when you want to use it. I was hopeful I had missed something on the description and that there was a rechargeable battery but unfortunately this is not the case. This was me being hopeful, not a confusing write-up.

It comes with a few attachments to help direct the air flow over the surface of what you’re trying to clean. The most helpful attachment, to me, is the round nozzle, but all of them have their uses.

I took it to my office where we have an abundance of dirty keyboards that need to be cleaned, and I set to work. I was expecting it to do a mediocre cleaning job, but it gave me a very pleasant surprise and blew air with plenty of force to clean out the clumps of dust that collect under the keys. More importantly, though, the power didn’t diminish like what tends to happen with canned dusters as they get cold, and there was no problem with frost buildup either.

So far, this is proving to be a useful and helpful tool. It produces enough force to get the job done without losing power, and it leaves no residue behind.

title: can I have half my money back please?
text:
I might be spoiled by Amazon's 6.99 downloads, because after finishing this game within a week of purchasing it I don't feel like it's a good value at all. Of course, this is comparing it to same-priced games like Burger Shop 2 and Monarch the Butterfly King, games that not only suck you in but are able to provide enough game to keep you playing for weeks straight. Pure Hidden is fun, it's not addicting to me because I don't find picture-find games addicting, but it is a game that I've enjoyed playing. The scenes which hide the pictures are different than what you find in a typical picture find game. The main pictures are gorgeous. I would even say they are works of art that one might frame and put on their wall. They aren't basic scenes with images of items cut out and scattered all over the place, rather they are well thought out and designed to cleverly hide the items within them, making them quite challenging. So far I've had to use the cheat tool to find at least one of the items in almost all of the scenes.

Unfortunately, I feel like the overall setup of the game was a total miss. Working to complete your gallery of scenes that you have finished (which you can install as a desktop background after you do) has nice appeal, but there is A LOT of filler in between the picture-find scenes, which consists of mini-games and mini-puzzles, some of which are completely pointless. For example, the "decorate your bathroom" activity--this one shows up multiple times as a "mini-game" but each time you're only given an option of one item to be put in a predetermined place, and ding, you're done for that one and it moves you on to the next puzzle. Totally pointless. Some of the mini-games have a really neat concept, like bursting the bubbles to play a song, but there is no goal whatsoever, and after about 15 seconds you get bored after realizing there's no challenge to it and hit next to move on, which you could have done in the first 5 seconds of the mini-game. A few of the mini-games are implemented with some really innovative ideas, like the "find the difference games" where you use your mouse to turn the 3D image and look at it from all sides. Now if there had been more of these in place of the pointless mini-games, then I think Pure Hidden would have been much more fulfilling. Unfortunately, Pure Hidden seemed to end as soon as it started. Overall, if you have 6.99 to spend and you're trying to find a game that will keep you engaged for more than a week, keep looking. Amazon has tons of 6.99 game downloads that last an eternity compared to this one.

Our Siamese wants only canned food, but she gets fussy when it's not these gravy and sauce ones. So, we're worried for her too. We've done some study on this and apparently the Friskies Classic Pates have only approx. 8 carbs per can, compared to approx. 14 in these gravy/sauce ones. So, we've decided to get them off the dry food altogether, get them on the Friskies Classic Pates and share some of our chicken and turkey with them occasionally too. First design review: For the price, it seems like a great tripod, but..., it was falling apart in the new bags it came in, so expect to locktite all screws, including the one holding the QD head to the ball section. And speaking of, the ball was way too tight for anyone to move without tools and that's with the tightening knob totally unscrewed. Sigh..

And the way this is sewn-in, there's not a good way to get it back together. So while the tripod (new design) is an exceptional design, the bag..., well..., this one's unusable now and I just took the thing out of the box for the first time to review it. Nice otherwise though, so it might be worth the $20 or so to have someone sew in a sturdy YKK zipper or something like that. title: Best headphones for the gym and doing random things around the apartment with I have ever used!
text:
I've been wanting to write a review for this for a long time but kept forgetting. I've put these through hell and I've had them ever since they first came out with the X2's. They are by far the best headphones I have ever used. I bought them not from Amazon but from Best Buy. Maybe Amazon is selling slightly used ones to have all these bad reviews? I don't know but just a guess.

Pair the headphones to your phone and hold the middle button down for 5 seconds to power down. All you gotta do then is hold the middle button down to turn on until the lady says "power on", let go of the button when she says this -- and boom -- "head phones connected". Very very easy.

I use it mainly for the gym and doing stuff around my apartment. I sweat like crazy and they still hold up like a champ. They fit so well into your ears they are completely locked in. Sound quality is very good and they are also very loud if you like to blast music like me (rap, metal, anything sounds good with these). Bass is solid for headphones. Don't really understand all the negative reviews on this but I have had these for at least 2-3 years and they are holding up perfectly.

If you buy these DEFINITELY take the time to watch a YouTube video on how to fold the cord with the brackets they give you so it fits nicely around the back of your head. Very simple and doesn't take long, you only have to do it once and you're good.

Only complaint is VERY VERY rarely you won't hear anything when you hold down the middle button and you have to plug the charger in and press the middle button 9 times and repeat this process until you hear "power on". Usually takes a few tries but this has rarely ever happened so I still give 5 stars for these headphones.

Don't listen to these reviews and go out and try it for yourself. They really are the GOAT and I have tried a lot of headphones.

title: Well-made leash with waist belt that allows a pet owner to walk or run with their pet hands free & has two handles for control
text:
This is a well-made dual-handle leash that permits a pet owner to walk or run with their dog (or cat) hands free. The waist belt is adjustable to 42" and the leash is attached to that belt. The bungee cord is relatively strong but if a large dog pulls, there is a potential of throwing the walker/runner off balance.

On one hand I like that the leash slides along the waist belt but on the other hand it can be dangerous when a pet runs in front or off to the side of the owner and does not stay in one place. When I used this, the belt slide easily along the waist. This is also well-made and the clasp is easy to clip onto the leash or halter. There are also two handles for when more control is needed.

title: UPDATE: died too soon  ...
text:
UPDATE: DIED after 2 months of use. I'm not a heavy or careless user of this kind of stuff -- this was plugged into a connector on my nightstand that also handled a mini-USB cable for my bluetooth speaker, and wasn't moved around at all. I tested it initially with my iPad Pro and my iPhone, but after the initial testing, it was used ONLY for charging my iPhone 6s usually 3 times per week or so. The first 6 weeks, it worked perfectly, and I was thrilled with it. Unfortunately, it started malfunctioning after 6 weeks (lights flashing randomly); after 8 weeks of use, it no longer worked at all. CANNOT recommend. Sorry.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've been living with this for about 10 days and I've had a chance to use it with my new-ish iPad Pro 9.7" and iPhone 6S.

So far, no problems at all. Functions just like the original cable except this one is longer and has some extra features -- aluminum housing on both ends is much more "solid" than the plastic and everything is well secured with no manufacturing defects that I could find.

Probably the best part of this cable is the LED light that tells you where your device is in the charging process. Pulsing red means it's charging; flickering green means it's almost done; solid green means it's 100%. The solid green light stays on for awhile (haven't been able to time it precisely as it seems to vary a little from charge to charge -- I'm thinking maybe a couple of hours or so before it goes off; then it stays off unless something "wakes it up" (a notification, a phone call, etc.). I charge the phone on my nightstand and I've had no problem with brightness, but then I sleep like a rock once I get to sleep and it didn't keep me awake, either. Some folks might have a problem, though, because the light is rather bright.

It fits just fine with my Speck case on the iPhone and the MoKo ultra-light case on the iPad.

I actually like this enough that I'll be ordering another one before I make my annual trip back home for the holidays so I can charge both devices at once. It's a nice cable, well made, great length, and I can tell by looking at it whether my device is finished charging.

title: A big improvement over the Smokin' Buds
text:
When my iPod buds finally died on me, I decided I wanted in-ear 'phones. However, I was short on cash, so I decided against the Shures, Etymotics, and the like. I saw the Smokin' Buds in a store for $[...], and gave them a shot.

First off, the sound wasn't terrible. It was at least on par with the Apple buds. I had problems with the fact that the sleeves wouldn't stay put in my ears for any reason, slipping out almost as soon as I'd inserted them. In addition, the cord was rather thin, and anytime it rubbed against my clothing, or heaven forfend, my jacket's zipper, it would create enough noise to drown out my music. The nail in the coffin was the small chrome ring on the left bud. I had foolishly thought it was structural, but when it popped loose it turned out to be merely ornamental.

I took them back for a refund, and sent off a letter to the company expressing my dissatisfaction with their product. Much to my surprise, I was invited to try another pair, with the promise that improvements had been made and I was sure to find them more to my liking.

The buds that arrived in the mail were the Full Metal Jackets. The difference in construction is night and day. Where the bulk of the Smokin' Buds is plastic, these are aluminum. The sleeves never slip from my ears. The cord is far more durable, and thicker as well.

The sound was quite boomy when I first tried them, but I let them run at high volume for 24 hours on static to loosen them up. This helped quite a bit, and the sound continues to improve. It's still bottom-heavy, but turning off the EQ function on my nano helped balance it out. I really like that I can run my nano at half volume and still hear everything clearly. In fact, I would caution against running them at full volume while they're in, as I'm certain one would suffer hearing damage. My battery life has improved tremendously. I'm very happy with the sound and the comfort of these buds. I can't think of a better set of earphones for the price... and the warranty is first-rate.

9 February 2008: I sent my FMJ's back for a warranty repair, which turned out to be a warranty replacement. The jack on my 9mm FMJ's had developed a short, and was causing the left 'bud to cut in and out.

I received an RMA number within moments of contacting them at their website, [...], and while I paid for shipping the 'buds back, they replaced them immediately, free of charge. Not only did they replace them with a new set, they sent the 11mm FMJ's. The jack is a bit longer, in order to provide better strain relief, I suppose. Otherwise, the build quality is identical. More importantly, the sound is far better balanced top to bottom, and while the bass is still great, it no longer dominates the sound spectrum as it did on my 9mm's.

In short, the 9's are really good, and you can't get anything better (in my opinion) at the price, but the 11's are worth the extra money. All the things that made my experience such a positive one with the 9's is improved with the 11's. Definitely a 5-star rating.

title: Confused game, bad controls
text:
This game is a hybrid of games we've all played before but it makes for an overall confused experience because of that. It is an interesting idea to take the best games and sort of mix them up though. It's got the focus button and combat cover system of Gears of War along with RPG elements in it and button mashing/timed events too.

I'm not a big fan of the "mic" commands interface since I don't have a mic on my computer it makes for an awkward unnecessary element in my mind. I'm forced to push the tab button and then select a command with the F button all while trying to blast the bad guys. Trying to pick the right comment to get what you want out of teammates is more of a tedious chore than any fun and their usually phlegmatic responses don't improve it. Having to watch for the comment button to move forward I guess forces you to be attentive. Even if I did have a mic button it's just too weird to talk to myself out loud while I'm playing a game. Hope they drop this part if there is a second game.

Also this is just not a PC game, it's really an afterthought port. It's painfully evident from the first time you start the game. The controls are default Xbox control mapped. Once you change the settings to mouse/keyboard(MKB) it's another painful surprise that the mapping seems odd. Spacebar and F are the enter and exit as well as action buttons with the mouse being standard point/shoot. I wish they could have done more work with the mouse wheel/wheel buttons as far as switching weapons, etc.

As far as combat it's pretty standard GOW stuff, cover, shoot etc. I wish there was the option to use the grenade as a separate button as it is you have to use 1234 to switch to grenade throw it then switch back to your shooter. The weapons are pretty standard which is disappointing in such a futuristic game a bit of imagination there would have been nice.

There are too many cut scenes in this game, thankfully they had the good sense to make them largely optional. It feels like you are just watching a CG movie, 3-4 cut scenes in one long sequence.

This game could have been much better but there are too many elements that take away from the flow of the action, which is what this game is at heart: an action game. The RPG elements via the command menu are unnecessary to me and poorly executed. When not in combat the character interactions/interaction menu is uninteresting and annoying. The whole trust system via making the right comments and actions is another unnecessary.

Graphics are pretty standard, nothing spectacular but nothing terrible.

I wouldn't recommend this at it's current price, if you can wait until there is a sale or simply wait a month or two and get it when it's at the correct price: 20 bucks or less.

I like this keyboard and mouse combo a lot--especially the smooth-as-silk mouse. I like to use a good sound card as I have ears that work and I can tell the difference. If you do not hear well and/or you are not good with differentiating sounds, use a cheap USB headset.

title: The screws are the worst!
text:
As convenient as this product makes hooking up networking cables, the cheap screws that come with this wall plate make installation a nightmare.

Do yourself a favor, if you have an extra light switch plate laying around, use those screws instead. I've installed two of these ethernet wall plates into two different low voltage mounting brackets. There are no threads in these mounting brackets. You're essentially creating the threads as you go. This necessitates a greater amount of torque and the screw heads are shallow. If using hand tools, this will require immense amounts of force to prevent stripping the heads. Normally, only a small, flat blade screwdriver is all that is required. But this installation works best if you have a powered screwdriver that will provide the necessary torque.

If you can run the screws in and out prior to installation, it may prevent some headaches. I did something similar to the first low voltage mounting bracket I purchased too.

You'll also find that if you have some screws from an existing light switch plate, that they have a deeper slot and are half the length. The provided screws were much longer than necessary. I replaced the screws on the second wall plate I installed after backing out the originals with a set of pliers after the heads were damaged.

To put this into context, I have the right tools and do more DIY than most other people I know.

title: Super easy to change this tailgate latch out
text:
Super easy to change this tailgate latch out. All in all the swap out took maybe 15 minutes at most (just latch assembly). It was really easy to swap out the key tumbler from the old latch.

The only issue I had and it could be a manufacturing issue or an install issue. I don't think it was install issue as I have installed low voltage wiring for 20 years and know how to run it properly etc. The issue could come from the factory as I have had some new wiring (just out of the package) damage from the factory. It is also possible it could have come from the installation activities. Let me clarify the issue was the included RCA cord and not the camera assembly, the cable was simply bad.

As always test the system before installing it permanently. It was a super easy fix for me, throw away the old wire and grab another RCA cable which I had in my electrical spare parts bin. I did not ask for a replacement from Amazon as it was way to easy for me to grab a new cable. I had the spare parts and the spare cable was a little higher quality (braided shielding and thicker diameter). My experience over the years with how often bad wiring occurs tells me very few people would experience this issue. Since the issue could have been me, the manufacturing of the cable or a combination of all, I have not taken any stars away.

The Camera (image) looks good, well as good as I would want. I installed this into my 2012 F150 work truck The install took 4 1/2 hours total. That total was also including installing an [[ASIN:B000C19DNM Pop & Lock PL8250 Power Tailgate Lock for Ford (For tailgate with OEM lock)]]. Since the wiring for both had to be done to the same areas of the passenger compartment, I elected for the an all at once installation. I am a little more picky than some on running my wiring, again due to my experience over the years. I would estimate most folks could do this within a couple of hours if they are familiar with their vehicle and accustomed to wiring electronics, and have a good set of tools to work with.

Oh this also was a 45+ year old man crawling around on the ground running wiring and so forth. I did not have a lift to facilitate the process which would have greatly sped up the installation process. Plus saved me throwing out several Danny Glover, Lethal Weapon quotes. :P If you have to ask go watch the movie bonus points if your 45+ and can relate once you watch it.

The instruction are lacking if your a novice, regarding the change out of the latch assembly. Its really just 2 bolts and slide the old one out and the new one in. If the new unit seems awkward to get back in slightly pull the handle as if opening the latch when trying to reinstall it.

It took a few minutes of fiddling to get the camera where I wanted it set. (rotation within the latch assembly) and I followed the advise of the instructions to put some silicone on the back of the camera housing between it and the plastic assembly. This secures the camera in the desired rotation and also reinforces the retaining clips ensuring your camera doesn't fall out.

I did notate the handle was slightly harder to pull to release the tailgate. That however was after the electronic lock assembly was installed. In a test fitting prior to that, it performed just as the original did. So IMO this product works perfectly and the harder pull was that of the power locking assembly.

I would 100% buy this product again.

I am super pleased with my purchase and the product in general. I elected this as a more factory looking camera.

title: Super large with some drawbacks (for me) and some pluses
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Keyboards are subjective - everyone will have a different opinion based on personal preference. Frankly, this is not among my preferences, but that is based on the oversized keys and the large footprint of the keyboard. I did not subtract a star for those - it was the way each key wobbled that caused me to give it the rating that I did.

Here are a few observations as well as why I personally do not care for it. First, I am an old geezer and am set in my ways. After using laptops for literally decades I had a difficult time getting accustomed to the size of this keyboard. To be fair, I feel the same way about normal desktop keyboards, but this one is MUCH larger and after an hour I had to disconnect it.

Second, there is almost no tactile feedback on key presses. Surprisingly (to me) I was not as put off by that, and I am guessing that using virtual keyboards on tablets (and smart phones) has weaned me off of that feature.

The lights are a nice feature. While I touch type, I had to keep looking at the keys on this thing because I was literally lost by the size and in a dim room I needed to see what I was pressing because what I thought I was typing and what was showing up on my screen were different. Long story short - I could easily become used to that aspect of the keyboard.

One test I put all keyboards through is to see if there is key bounce - when you press and release a key quickly and there are multiple characters. This did not exhibit that problem, so I have a lot of confidence in the underlying mechanics and electronics. And when I was hitting the right keys this keyboard did keep up with me, so that is another point in its favor.

Bottom line: if you are accustomed to full size keyboards and have BIG hands this may, in fact, be the keyboard for you. It's mechanically sound, but if I am any indication, it's not for everyone.

title: I really wanted to like this game.....
text:
I've played the Harry Potter Game Boy Advance games on the DS....as well as HP 4,5 and 6 on the DS platform. I was really looking forward to this game and I have to say....it was a HUGE let down for me.

CONS:
* From the start, the graphics are mediocre. The characters still don't speak, there are subtitles for the conversation.

* The lack of conversation wouldn't have been so bad...if there was SOME background music. I thought I needed to adjust the settings on my DS because it was so quiet. But no, there is no background music. The only background sound that I have found, is when you are trying to cast a spell. Not even your decoy detonators make noise (I know, cause I wasted a bunch....couldn't tell if they were going off!!)

* The controls are COMPLETELY wonky! You are given an invisibility cloak....which is completely useless. I found that even while invisible AND standing still, the death eaters still walked right over and found me. Potion making is ridiculous! I was making a potion and I was told to shake a beaker up and down.....sounds simple right? So I shook it up and down and nothing was happening to the bar on the side (it fills up as you perform each task.) I lost time and had to start the potion all over again. I repeated this 5 times...and I still shook the beaker the same way (as instructed by the game) and for some reason, it worked on the last try. CRAZY! I found it awkward to try to walk thru this game using the stylus. I kept touching the up/down/let/right button by accident and as some of your spells are there.....I would end up unintentionally casting a spell and losing power....and sometimes brought unwanted death eater attention upon myself.

* The levels are long and you cannot save in the middle of them. The game only saves when you reach checkpoints. This wouldn't have been a terrible thing....IF my game had not frozen in the middle of one of these levels.

* I just found this game to be flat out BORING compared to the other HP games.

I really wanted to like this game. I lost count of how many times I decided to give it yet ANOTHER chance and start it over. Can't do it again. Already listed this game for sale.

title: Returned to Canon for repair for out-of-the-box sensor mis-calibration
text:
Tried to write a review of this on DP Review, but their over-the-top, religious zealots banned one post for using the word "gobsmacked" (when describing my experiences with the first 6D) and another post because of the word "pissed," (after calling Canon and finding out I would have to send it to them at my own cost) both banned claiming violation of their "rule 6," for "profanity." So..., I'll make sure my review is somewhere that people can or might see it and be able to use for their determination if this camera is right for them.

For the price, overall, it's NOT a good deal. Uses the same processor as the Rebels (ie; T7i) and the same articulating screen. Also, the focus points are all bunched-up in the center of the sensor, so a FF sensor is kind of meaningless for AF when you only cover 40% of sensor and it's all in the center? Also, the sensor is a step back from the older 6D. It claims more MP's, but really, if it doesn't have the DR of the original camera it's supposed to replace, then I say it's a step back. Yes, it has DPAF, but that's a function of the processor, not the sensor. So it's basically a weather sealed (maybe) FF T7i. Except without the flash...

Honestly, the T7i feels like a toy, but the few weeks I had and tested it, it was rained on, snowed on and I generally beat the camera up. It took the abuse with zero issues and the DPAF worked brilliantly. Photo's rivaled that of this 6D MII.

First day I had the 6D Mark II, something seemed wonky, but an update of the firmware to 1.0.4 fixed the weird switch issue. Nothing could fix the wildly un-calibrated ISO issue though. After talks with Canon repair center, they said to ship it to them. Since it was after the 30-days I have to return something at BB, I had no other choice.

So why did I send it in? The ISO calibration was WAY off from the get go. Orders of magnitude off. The orig 6D had me gobsmacked (oh my..., there's that profanity!) with it's low-noise at very high ISO. That was unbelievable. This camera though couldn't touch a 5D MII, a 70D or the T7i. Same lens, same coverage (making allowance for 1.6CF of the 70D/T7i), same shutter speed, same aperture, the three test subjects were 1200ISO, with the 6D MII, to get the same exposure, I was at 3200 and higher ISO. Kind of the opposite of what you'd expect, especially considering my opposite experiences with the original 6D. Esp from a $1600+ NEW camera/sensor. And sending back to Canon means YOU Pay the shipping to them. And insurance. So roll in $35 more into the price of the camera.

Some will say just a fluke and that these things happen. They do. But with all the issues combined in a camera that is sub-par to a $750 rebel in almost every aspect, well..., I say stay away until the price comes down to a point that it makes sense to buy a FF rebel with (alleged) weather sealing and no flash.

Crunchy cookie sized treats that smell good, look good, have great ingredients, priced well, and are packaged nicely in a pressure zip durable plastic bag. We have quickly become a Wag family!

https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07V9Z4GZW

I may add this into my regular orders, and I would totally feel comfortable giving this as part of a pet themed gift, or as a bag of snacks to have on hand for any visiting doggos. Or to buy for purpose of donation (doesnt break the bank!). I dont rate on price, but it is truly refreshing that these are healthy, quality treats that are really reasonably priced. So many are boutique priced, and these are absolutely as good as those kinds.

I also greatly appreciate a well done product page. There is plenty of information, the pictures are clear, and they have bonus question/answer section that further makes me feel comfortable to purchase Amazon Brand Wag treats for my babies.

title: Nothing Special
text:
Let me preface this review with saying that I love the Spectrum Noir markers. Have had both generations and recommend them to everyone. They are easy to use and a good value. On the other hand, I am not so "gobsmacked" about the new line of pencils. I bought the complete set because I am an illustrator and I like to have full sets of the tools I use. First off I was put off by the fact that there are 5 tins to sort through to find a color. I'm sure they did this, so folks could buy a tin at a time, but it easy to keep flipping open lids and looking around for just the right color you want. The pencils also fit very snuggly in the boxes and it is difficult to get them out sometimes.
As for the "creaminess" of said pencils, I would say there are some inconsistencies in that as well. Some of the Floral colors are really soft and creamy, some of the browns and grays are hard and scratchy and then there are some that are just so waxy you can't lay down two colors on top of each other.
If you are a rubber stamper or crafter that plans to use them, you will probably be fine with these. They seem to be geared more to that kind of audience. The price is right for what you get. I had no trouble sharpening the few I used. No breakage like I have encountered with the Prismacolor set I've had for 10 years. The blending solution I suspect is just Gamsol which most stampers already have if they've been using pencils before. I was able to achieve the same results using the Prismacolor pencils I had over the markers.
I will say their customer service rocks because they are going to allow me to send these back. This is a great company to deal with, I just think they kind of missed the mark with these.

title: Easy to use one handed. Good for wide open vistas, not great for details
text:
I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.

These are excellent earbuds. The sound is open, spacious, clear, and pleasant. I have listened to music for hours on these, and my ears don't get tired at all. Here's what I like and don't like.

The sound is open, with sparkling high frequencies and tight, precise lows. The highs sparkle so much that some listeners might think that the sound is too bright. I'm pretty happy with it. The midrange is clear, voices very easy to understand. The lows are not at all boomy, and not as powerful as earbuds that advertise things like "deep powerful bass." But the bass is solid, and for music that has lots of bass energy, these earbuds let it all come through. Overall I think the sound is very accurate, uncolored, and not at all leading to ear-fatigue. I'm very, very pleased with the sound. Pretty sweet.

The product packaging is pretty silly. It's completely overdesigned, with an outer box that separates to allow you to get to an inner tray. I puzzled over the package for about 3 minutes trying to figure out how to get into it, before I discovered a diagram on the side panel of the box. After I successfully extricated the earbuds ...

The plug has a novel oversized swivel that allows it to attach either straight or at right angles to your sound source. It's clever, but I prefer plugs that are visibly more protective of the cord. There's no bendy thing where the cord joins the oversized plug, so I'm concerned that over time the wire might break at the join. We'll see. Whether the swivel is straight or right angled, it's a large plug that I think might be uncomfortably large with some phones or MP3 players. I'm using it with a laptop computer, and it sometimes gets in the way a bit.

In the middle of the cable is a volume control barrel. Just like the plug, it's a classy-looking silvery metal color. But what it earns in form it loses in function, as the volume control slider is very difficult to operate. I have some earbuds that cost only 20% what these cost, and they have a volume control slider that very much easier to use than we have here. Nevertheless, the slider does a good job of controlling the volume when I can get my fingers to operate it.

The earbuds themselves are interesting because they have rather large metal pieces that support the part that fits in the ear. My first reaction was that they would be uncomfortably heavy, or that they might fall out of the ear, but they work remarkably well. I've listened for hours, and had to reposition the earbuds only occasionally.

The cable is typical plastic-coated cable that's heavier than some other earbuds have. It feels rugged, and it doesn't tangle easily. A cloth-wrapped cable would be much nicer still.

The earbuds come with a case that stores the earbuds and the included airplane adaptor. It's a rather large case -- it doesn't fit well into your pocket (for traveling), but does protect the earbuds very well. There's also a second very small drawstring bag, which I assume is for traveling, but it's just a bit too small and stiff to do that job well.

title: Inexpensive, Basic Lens Protection
text:
A UV filter on a lens can be a cheap and effective way to protect your expensive glass. Some of these filters are better than others, and this one is on the lower end of the scale. That said, it's worth its asking price.

Most digital cameras already have decent UV filtering built in so there's not a lot of sense to getting a UV filter for that purpose. However, these filters do have a very important role - they provide very inexpensive protection for the lens, for both dirt and scratches. An inexpensive filter like this is a lot less expensive to replace than a lens that cost hundreds of dollars.

My complaint with this filter is the same as with other inexpensive filters I have used. It's reflective, and in certain situations I can get reflections between the lens and the filter that can mess up an otherwise good image. A fine example is when photographing trains or oncoming cars that have turned on their headlamps. In those cases, this filter interferes and causes very noticeable reflections when the angle is just right.

The majority of the time, this filter is fine protection for my lens and I shoot with it in place. However, there are times when it is a detriment and I remove it for those cases. A more expensive filter that cuts down reflections is a better choice for those situations. However, those filters cost a lot more in most cases.

This is a decent UV filter for the price. It provides good basic protection for the lens on which it is attached and the price is reasonable. There are cases where it's more of a problem than a help, though, and for those cases it is easy enough to remove.

title: Play it your first time around the block
text:
A lot of people say this is the greatest game in the series. It seems a lot of "impartial" game review magazines and Web sites say the same thing. I can't judge if this is hype or if it's just me, though.

First off, I do not fault the graphics like so many people do. Those who do fault it for this reason are not true gamers. A good game transcends its own graphics. I've said before, even if a game was 8-bit, as long as the story was enthralling, I'd be fine. A real gamer recognizes that aspect.

However, there's a lot of this game that is bad. On to the gist of the review.

A friend of mine has faulted this game as "Final Anime." Truly, it did take on a lot of anime-esque themes and character personalities. I use Cloud as an example. He never grows as a character from the start of the game to the end. No, he doesn't. Get over it. He is the same brooding, emo kid at the end of the game that he was when it started. Not to mention, there's a "huge" reveal about his backstory on disc 2 that's reminiscent of anime, where it diverts from the main story for episodes and episodes and does. not. die. Not to mention, the excessive flashbacks, which, I know are not new to the series, which just play up how underdeveloped the characters are.

Onto the gameplay. Each character is completely indistinguishable from the others. The only differences are pixel sets and limit breaks. Magic should be based on class. In this game, every character can equip any kind of magic. Stats are so similar between characters who are supposed to be fighters and those who are supposed to be mages. There's no distinction between them. The materia system cripples the game because anyone can be a healer or a status magic user.

Sephiroth. Most definitely not the coolest villain in the series. People think he's cool because he walked through fire with a huge effing sword. That does not equate to cool. You want a good villain? Go with FF6's Kefka. He actually DID destroy the world and created a religion unto himself.

I fault the character development the most in this game. No one grows. No, they don't. Deal with it. Real character development can be found with characters from FF6 like Locke Cole. He swears to himself he will never let the fate of his fiancee Rachel fall upon any of his friends.

Also, Aeris isn't the first main character in the series to die. That goes to FF5's Galuf.

Give the game a shot if you're an RPG newbie. It might hold you for a repeat, but it also might not. Take this game with a grain of salt. I own it for completion's sake.

title: It’s early, but I’m impressed so far
text:
Among others, I have a Great Dane and an English Mastiff. The mastiff is only 10 months old, and nowhere near full grown, but has an enormous head, and thus enormous jaws. Nearly every toy I’ve purchased for him in the last 7 months has been utterly and completely destroyed in a few hours. There’s a couple toys that last a few weeks, but I had to stop giving him rope chews. He loves them, and used to just shred them for easy vacuuming every day. Recently he started eating the shredded rope, so I can’t let him have those, and went looking for something cloth-like without a squeaker** in it.

I decided to give these frisbee like things a try. He’s been ripping and tearing at that thing for several of the last 24 hours, and there’s not a mark on it, and no holes in it. He’s played tug with his friend the Great Dane, and they haven’t managed to damage it, even on the corners.

I bought 2 to start with, and today purchased 2 more. He will destroy it eventually, so I want to have a new one available every time to keep him chewing the RIGHT things.

**For those wondering why I won’t buy toys with squeakers in them: the noises they make are deliberately designed to mimic the sound of a small animal in pain or distress. This can reinforce the natural prey drive that every dog Osborn with. In dogs with a moderate to high prey drive, when that drive is stimulated by sound, it can increase the drive, and endanger smaller animals in the home. Since I have 2 chihuahuas, and neighbors who let their cats roam free, I prefer to discourage the prey drive, and reduce the risk.

The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.

title: Not My Dog's Favorite Treats but They Pass
text:
Dogs love treats. They love food in general, as any dog owner knows, but they particularly love dog treats, especially those that are meaty and pungent with a scent that only a dog could appreciate. Other treats, well, they get less excited over and a prime example of the latter is Good N Fun Smoky Barbecue Flavor Treats.

These beef hide treats are solid in structure and are long and cylindrical in shape. They are thin, so there isn’t a whole lot of treat in each piece. They are designed for long lasting chewing action, and that is their primary purpose. Give one of these treats to your dog and it could very well keep him/her occupied for ten, fifteen, or more minutes. This is very different than other dog treats, most of which are gone within seconds after feeding.

Good N Fun do last longer than other treats, and this is good. But the negative is that my dog just doesn’t get that excited over them. He hears me say the word treat, and he normally reacts with anxious anticipation. But he just doesn’t get into these dog treats. He doesn’t grab them vigorously from my hands, like he does with his favorite treats. And when he has the treats in his mouth, he will often drop them after a minute of chewing once something distracts him. The treats are just not that appealing, at least not compared to the best dog treats on the market.

This isn’t to say that these dog treats are a total bust. My dog doesn’t find them very noteworthy, but he does eventually give in and finish them off and the longer than normal time to chew means he is preoccupied longer than with other dog treats. If you happen to have a young dog or other dog that has a habit of chewing, the fact that the treats are chewy can also mean your furniture and other valuables are a little safer.

My dog loves his dog treats, but he is less than thrilled with Good N Fun Smoky Barbecue Flavor Treats. They have enough going for them to reward a small recommendation overall, but be prepared for a less than excited reaction when you feed these to your dog.
