title: Great performance
text:
EVGA ftw3 version runs super quiet. Can barely hear it run. At highest settings @ 6880 x 1440 resolution, it never runs hotter than 65c. As to whether 2080ti is worth it in general:

Increase in FPS performance- Too many people judge the 2080ti's merit on raw FPS numbers, saying its only x amount of percent greater in performance than the 1080ti. so its not worth it. But what they completely miss is that its not just about the raw numbers. Its about how those numbers translate into the EXPERIENCE of adding/using that component. The performance of the 2080ti is so much smoother, more effortless and frustration free, than the previous generation, that it was worth it for me to make the change.

Alernative Sli option- I tried 1080ti sli for about a month, it didnt affect the quality of my experience in a meaningful way. The presentation is still jittery and stuttering , making for a distracting experience. Support for SLI is inconsistent and it demands more power and space, creates alot more heat and noise. You can clearly see the poor quality of performance in side by side comparisons on youtube. Judge for yourself. Again, its not all about the FPS. A perfect analogy would be to cars- most high end races cars have respectable 0-60 mph speeds, but the experience and qualty of performance arent the same.

Price argument: Just because its expensive and someone cant afford it doesnt mean its a 1 star product. Check the quality, time and effort the reviewer put into the review and judge for yourself. It takes money, time and expensive R&D to make products such as these. Im not going to argue that its not expensive. It is. But consider that it beats two 1080ti SLI in quality of performance, then you realize it isnt. If you are salty that you cant afford it, try skipping some meals and dropping some vices and prioritize things differently. Seems everyone wants free things these days. I wonder if they would work without compensation.

Conclusion: Sure its expensive, but if you can afford it and you want quality performance, not just eye popping FPS numbers, which can be meaningless, get the 2080ti. Some just cant see the difference and thats fine. But for those who can afford it and have more discerning eyes, the upgrade is a must. My only complaint? It cant make poorly coded, inefficient games like Kingdom Come run better at the highest settings on a 6880 x 1440 setup. (Runs nearly every other game at the highest setting flawlessly at these high resolutions) Might have to wait for the next generation for that. Because of that and the "high" price it doesn't get a top recommendation but a very high recommendation.

title: Wrong instructions and wobbly, but still fun to use.
text:
Before ordering this telescope, I researched the difference between reflector and refractor telescopes. The last telescope I had was a hand-me-down (I forget which brand) refractor telescopes. I've developed a strong passion for everything beyond earth, so I looked forward to using this telescope--my first reflector telescope.

Because the telescope requires assembly, I pulled out the instructions...and became very confused. While some of the parts looked similar to what was in the box, I quickly realized the instructions were for a completely different model. Even if these were the right instructions, the photographs provided were taken by a camera and not the clearest quality; good assembly instructions usually have computer-generated images or diagrams, not photographs taken by a camera. The rest of the instruction manual was a general guide on using telescopes, though a much better quick-start guide can be found easily online.

So, with some trial and error, and a lot more time than I anticipated building the telescope, I finally got it assembled. And just in time too, because the moon had just crossed the window of the room I build the telescope in, and the moon was in great view. The opportunity also let me play around with the features of the telescope. It's not very easy to use because the stand is *very* wobbly. The counterweights are too much for the tripod, and the tripod should have used a better, more sturdy material. The dials and weights are easy to use, but the tripod makes everything longer to set up because the view won't always stay while moving.

Despite all that, it's super fun to use. It comes with decent eyepieces to play around with; I didn't know how much of a difference eyepieces can make. With this telescope, I was able to view details of the moon for the first time. It really is just a big ball of rock spinning around.

title: Groovy GPS when used with Fresh Maps update
text:
I first bought this GPS several months ago when Costco had it on sale but ended up returning it because I was not pleased with the time it took to recognize my location. More specifically, I would be on the Capital Beltway surrounding DC and the stern female voice would repeatedly tell me to make a U-turn. Impossible. I then used a friend's hand-me-down Magellan which would not hold a charge, not recognize the location and simply needed to be retired. Enter Amazon and their great price for the Navigon 2100 max. Since I'd read that the device was improved with the Fresh Maps update, I purchased Fresh Maps and I highly recommend you do the same if you're contemplating this beautifully sleek GPS.

If you have a PC, you are able to upgrade by connecting the GPS directly to your computer. If you have a Mac, then it's a little more complicated but so worth the effort. You need to remove the SD card from the GPS and transfer the downloaded software to the SD card with a card reader/writer and then reinsert the card into the GPS. I kept a backup of the original software on my hard drive just in case, but have had no need since the upgrade immediately worked. Now on to what I really like about this system.

The 4.3 inch screen is easier to view than the 3.5, particularly if you have many of the POI's selected for display. I first chose them all, then realized they obstructed my map because I'm in the DC metro area. Mine connects with a satellite in only a few seconds each time and reroutes immediately if I change my route. Previously, it would announce that it was rerouting, but it no longer does that, just does the work. Three choices for trip planning are fine enough for me, I tend to choose the Optimal Route. I love being able to select different destinations, too, if I'm going to different places. The address book is easy to access and locations are easier to save. Traffic support is a great asset and now comes free with this device -- I've been saved from many a jam and not have to be tuned into the radio for traffic reports on the 8's. I have the screen set to automatically change from day to night and have had no problem viewing the screen at any time. With the new software, you are able to turn off the GPS from the touchscreen in addition to the usual power button at the upper right hand edge. I love the 2D/3D view, especially when I'm approaching a multi-lane area and I'm unsure as to which lane I need to take. Two voice selections are fine for my needs, Dagmar is more pleasant, but the higher pitched Sarah gives the text to speech option (TTS), so that's the one I've selected. She's not very pushy, either, as some voices I've heard on GPS systems. In the pre-update version, her voice sounded more Germanic, I assume from its origin of Germany, but it's not as odd now. For me, this GPS is intuitive to use and I can make any adjustments from the touchscreen very quickly. I've yet to have a freeze of the system and it has always known where I was with one exception when I was off road on a gravel trail.

My only real criticism of this unit is the rigid cord which extends straight out of the bottom of the device, being so inflexible that I sometimes dislodge it when attaching the mount to the windshield. I'm not crazy about the mount either, but am trying to decide how to approach a new mounting system. I do not want the display obstructing my field of vision but am not ready yet to get a sandbag type dashboard mount. I'm thinking of constructing something myself using the little plastic disc which was included with this GPS system. Also included is the USB cord, but no AC power supply.

title: Acer Aspire: Everything We Want in a Computer
text:
Computers are an important part of life. I know, I know- we need to get away from electronics and try to return to the days when more personal interactions were the norm. But regardless of how you feel about the proliferation of electronics in everyday living, there is no denying that most of us need them to one degree or another. We are writers/bloggers in my home and need good machines to carry us through the day. And the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop is one excellent machine for everyday use.

Let’s start with the physical attributes. This Acer computer features a very large flat screen with excellent clarity, making it ideal for watching videos, television shows, etc. The keyboard and mouse are wireless, so there is no issue over wires getting tangled as you work. Best of all, the CPU is part of the monitor. There is no separate tower or other computing unit, and that means this computer is space efficient. All you need is a place wide enough to handle the width of the monitor. The keyboard is certainly different from the one I was using previously and it took some adjusting to get used to. But this is the case with any new keyboard and you know what?- the adjustment period for this keyboard was less than a day. In almost no time at all, my wife and I took to the change and had no further issues.

As for the set up, well, it doesn’t get much better than this. I can remember when it would take several hours and much frustration to set up a new computer. But with Acer Aspire, the set up was complete and the computer was ready to use in less than 10 minutes after removing it from the box! We actually scheduled some time in our day, thinking it was going to require a fair amount of time to complete everything. It was so fast I started to worry that I did something wrong. But that wasn’t the case- everything is pretty much ready to go, straight from the package.

Because of our writing and blogging, we often need to have multiple windows open at any given time. This was an issue with my wife’s laptop and it would often slow her computer to a crawl. With this Acer computer, there is no such problem. She can have ten separate windows open, along with Microsoft Word and Excel, and the speed is still as good as ever. Again, this is a definite plus, as computer speed is a top concern for us and many other computer users.

I always try to find something that needs improvement when I write a product review but with the Acer Aspire, I can think of only one thing, and it relates to the Office Suite. They give you Office Suite for a free trial but once the trial is up, you will have to purchase it yourself. Acer could easily make this improvement and while this type of criticism has really nothing to do with the functionality of the product itself, it is about the only issue I can find. Everything else about this computer is well above average.

Computers are essential to my household. We need our computers for writing, for the classes I teach, and other uses. With the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop, we have found a cutting- edge computing machine that fits our needs perfectly and has everything we desire. It’s an excellent computer that would look really good on your desktop and I recommend it when it comes time for your next pc upgrade.

title: Decent for the price
text:
I love this fitness tracker. I mainly bought it to start tracking my stress level and heart rate, and while I find that the watch itself is not always accurate, the app calculates your stats more accurately. For instance, while doing P90X, it said my heart rate was in the 90s. Uh, no. Though, the app said 140s, which yes, that's much more accurate. However, I honestly don't really care about that. I love getting the little "Move!" notifications, as it reminds me I've been sitting for too long and I need to get up and move around. I can already feel myself shaving inches off my hips by remaining more active. Plus, keeping an eye on my stress level and heart rate has helped me consciously lower both, and it even calculates your average sleep. I thought I was getting at least seven hours a night, but it's actually less, and I wouldn't have known that without the watch. This is due to the fact that I apparently have a lot of light sleep and barely any deep sleep. Ultimately, it serves as a loose reminder to take better care of myself, and even if it's not pinpoint accurate, that's enough for me to justify spending the money on it (bonus points for being able to take it into the shower after a workout!).

EDIT: Also, I find that the app drains the hell out of my phone battery. So I log out once I've logged most of my info for the day, then I log back in the next day to allow it to catch up. It still keeps all the information in the watch, so you don't lose anything, and you can save your phone's battery life.

title: Excellent experience and GOTY contender.
text:
As a long time video gamer who never owned a PlayStation, the Metal Gear Franchise was brand new to me. I immediately jumped into the game and enjoyed the unfamiliar narrative and game perspective. The cinematic scenes are wonderful and lead the story along well.
If you have never played a Metal Gear game, throw the following games in a blender, add ice, and enjoy:
1) Just Cause 2
2) Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
3) Farmville

The reasoning?
1 - The game has quite a bit of open world, wander around and have fun, but with objectives still tied.
2 - While you can be deadly and run-and-gun in this game (the path I'm taking more of), this game rewards you for being stealthy. You will spend half of your time planning and the half executing your plan.
3 - The game provides you a base to help in research new items and maintain a constant flow of materials and money to further your progress. While there isn't much of a grind to the game, I do find that I have to watch my funds and make decisions on what I want to progress on next.

Two cons for the PC version - no multiplayer as of yet. If multiplayer does matter to you, then I would recommend holding off until Konami announces that their multiplayer servers are stable. Second issue controlling your horse when using a keyboard and mouse. The riding experience is subpar as the controls for riding are not adjusted for WASD so your horse will not make good angular adjustments until you move your mouse in that specific direction. This is fine when running away, but makes life difficult when attempting to fire a weapon while riding.

Based on just the single player experience, MGS V:TPP is a worthy contender for Game of the Year (GOTY).

While HeartGold and SoulSilver will hold a special place in my heart as my favorites, Black 2 (I refer only to Black 2 in this review, though most commentary is transferable to White 2 as well) is a strong entry in the Pokemon series without a doubt,and may objectively be the best so far.

Game Freak made a surprising move in announcing "Black and White 2", as no games had ever had direct sequels before - immediately visiting a new region ought to have killed the game while it was still an idea. It made it through somehow though, and I'm glad it did, because these games are packed so full of new content I have no doubt that I got my money's worth. From the new storyline to new areas to the medal system (a nod to Steam's "Achievements" and the like), there's no doubting that Game Freak took pains to make this a world worth revisiting.

All the old favorites are present (all... what, 649 of them) and some Pokemon come in new forms as well. The new starting area is especially appreciated, as starting off exactly the same way B/W did would have started things off on an old, expired note. Also updated is the necessity of HMs - once a painful bane of a gamer's existence, they've been almost entirely eliminated from the main story, instead serving as paths to extra areas. And my are there extras, though I'd prefer not to say much about them to keep the review relatively spoiler-free.

The game starts slow as usual, and the graphics have received little update, always a weak point of the series. Likewise, the plot is thin (though in recent games, has shown some improvement, especially in B/W and here). However, combat is as finely-tuned as ever, and if you live around many other Pokemon fans, there is no end in the ways to compete. It's always a little harder on those living in Poke-isolation, and while wifi takes some steps to relieve that, the "Pal Pad" is always a burden.
Still, these are minor issues in comparison to the big picture. Pokemon has always been strong, and Black 2 is another, if surprising, improvement to the franchise.

title: Playable and time consuming, but not special
text:
This is a game that can definitely burn a number of hours as you build up forces and try to conquer the world. In style of play it most resembles Elemental or Civ V than other older turn-based 4X games.

I have to say that I liked elemenats of hte game, but could not call this a masterpiece. The standard for most fantasy 4X games is still Master of Magic. Yes, the graphics are terrible, but the shear number of races and spells and the addition of heroes made the game a huge step up compared to the other options. Age of Wonders tries to capture the same elements, but for me it never quite achieved the same elegance.

Warlock doesn't try to be as expansive as Master of Magic. There are only 3 races and no technology tree. The only research is for spells, and the research tree is rather linear, you see 5 options to research and from what I could see the system works by a "researched X spell and spell X+1 appears in the tree. The spells appear to follow a very linear tech tree.

Combat is not much different than Civ V, the lack of stacking makes it a bit more tactically than Civ IV, but it's still rather straightforward in execution.

Honestly, this feels like it could have been a lot better if more time had been spent expanding options. The lack of races, the lack of a tech tree, the linear nature of spell research, all leaft me thinking the game could be so much more.

But I love 4X games, so I still enjoy this one. It plays faster and smoother than Elemental, and while lacking in some elements, does not have the same balance issues that make Elemental nearly impossible to enjoy.

If you like 4X games, and like the idea of adding magic, this is worth trying. Otherwise, it will likely frustrate you.

title: Official SONY UHS-II
text:
I currently own 3 Sony Alpha cameras, and regularly record in 4K for work. Having a high quality fast card is important if you rely on your footage. That's why I generally only trust my paying jobs to Sony and Sandisk media. This is a real UHS-II card, as you can see in the picture attached. You can tell by the extra pins on the card, which are used for the UHS-II standard to boost the read/write speeds.
Of course, you can still read/write with a regular SD card reader, but you'll only get the benefits of the speed boost with a proper SD card port that supports the extra pins for UHS-II. Unfortunately, my desktop does not support this so I was unable to run benchmarks on the card to show you (it runs as a regular UHS-I with average speeds), but the camera is where it will make the most real-world difference, and most modern Sony cameras will have the support for this standard. If you write a lot of high bitrate 4K, especially with a Sony camera, this is the card for you!

title: WOW- PERFECT For Our Very Skittish Cat
text:
Our last cat was a short haired cat who almost never got anything in his fur that he could not clean out. Our current cat, however, is the polar opposite. She has baby fine fur which is long and resembles that of angora rabbits. She was not long haired when we rescued her as a kitten, but she quickly great to sport quite the long hair. The problem is she HAS to be outside. That is where she loves to be and not letting her out would probably cause total destruction of the house.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a rechargeable clipper, combs for different lengths, a recharger, a file, scissors, a comb, nail clippers and a cleaning brush.

CHARGER
This charger is a transformer base so it needs to be in an outlet with some room- not a narrow one.

CLIPPERS
These are very quiet. They have adjustment on them which takes you from to the skin almost to 2mm long.

COMBS
The combs that you add to this are like those for hair clippers. They raise the cut area to longer lengths

COMB AND SCISSORS
These allow for getting certain areas clean and combed and trimmed. They work well but are a bit large for our cat. She hates them and won't let them near her without trying to bite them.

FILE
This is a nice file for nails, but our cat hates it and won't let us near her with it.

HOW DOES THE CLIPPER WORK?
Amazingly, our cat sits very still when we trim her tummy and hind quarters with this set of clippers. She loves it. She lets us shave her belly and around her rear until we get too close to her private area and then she freaks. That is a miracle. This cat hates EVERYTHING having to do with cutting or maintaining her fur. However, this is the exception.

CHARGING
This took a few hours and will give me about five or six grooming sessions before I have to charge again. That is because I have to wait so long between grooming and between shaving different spots. The battery does run down if you don't use it for long periods, so be aware of that.

DO THEY TRIM THE FUR WELL?
The combs don't work well for our cat, but when we use just the clippers set on the highest setting with no combs, it works like a charm and trims her fur perfectly for summer time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this is a great set, the clippers is the main reason I got this. It works like a charm on the cat. She loves it and loves to be trimmed with it. Every other tool is attacked bitten and growled at.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a fabulous tool and I won't be without it.

title: A micro-managers dream come true
text:
This game was recommended to me by a friend who also loves real time simulation games. Next to the Simcity franchise, this is one of the most popular and well-received RTS games out there.

A little backstory... I started playing Sim Theme Park (1999) back in 2000. That was (and still is) a very fun simulation game. One of the best in my opinion. I feel the mixture of real-world accuracy and fun gameplay (even though very cartoony) was executed perfectly by the developers. Furthermore, the overall aesthetics and art style of the game are very appealing to me.

RT3, however, is a jumbled, overly-complicated mess in my opinion. The UI does not flow well, and the item menu layout makes it difficult to manage your park. Most importantly, there are just way too many options to play with! Everything (and person) in the park has a full-range of options to tweak... enough to make an OCD person go absolutely nuts, lol. I fully support real-world accuracy in these games, but I also understand that it's still a game, and I want to have fun playing it. And the developers definitely went full-tilt making RT3 as realistic as possible. Some people will no doubt love this, but I think that most people coming from Simcity or Sim Theme Park will find the game far too micro-manage-y.

The sandbox mode is fun, but since money is not involved, you quickly lose motivation playing it. What's the point if you can build anything you want, immediately? The campaign mode is not what I expected... I was thinking it was more along the lines of Sim Theme Park or Simcity where you start with a lump sum of money and an empty park, and you build your park from there, managing it along the way to keep a positive cash flow. Instead, the campaigns are somewhat preformed, giving you a basic park that you 'take-over' management of. Not very exciting in my opinion.

Overall, the game is not as fun as I had hoped for. If they allowed users to let the park run more autonomously (perhaps an 'auto-pilot' mode if you will) with the ability to tweak various items if needed, that would be better. Or, as an alternative, provide advice to the user on various aspects of the game (i.e. people find admission prices very cheap... people are not satisified with the quality of ice cream offered... etc). In it's current state, however, I don't want to go through my 5 hot dog stands and adjust the amount of mustard on my hot dogs.... and have to guess what the best selling price would be based on the insignificant amount of financial data the game provides real-time. The concept is great, but they just strayed too far in to the weeds without providing enough framework to allow the player to adequately adjust all of the options.

Those coming from Simcity- or Sim Theme Park-style games beware... you probably won't enjoy this one.

The graphics and art design especially are wonderful(i don't know what the crack smoker saying they looked like N64 was thinking), the sound design and music are great(i found myself humming along with the tunes after only 20 minutes), and the level design, as always, is impeccable.  The new controls are the real shining light here though.  Any review you read saying you will always see other FPS controls as second rate after this are true and i am not an old hand at FPS by any means(i can't stand the overrated Halo series).  However as a longtime  Metroid player i do have some gripes with a near flawless game experience.  For starters the default difficulty is Wind Waker easy(start on Veteran unless you've never played video games before).  The voice acting is very well done but the heavy rotation of the cliche 'Space Marines' had me gritting my teeth at times like the game designers were trying to match this up to Halo.  I almost felt like i was playing Fusion at times because Aurora keeps butting in to tell me where to go...uhh, excuse me, i though i turned the hints off.  I've always loved that the Metroid series Doesn't hold your hand like 95% of modern games do.  There is not as much isolation as before but it is still definitely more adventure than action.  i knew Retro wouldn't completely blow it.  The boss battles are things of strategic beauty(especially on the harder difficulties) and the creatures have such a beautiful, realistic synergy with their repective planets.  Using the ship is really fun(i wish there were more things to blow up though!) and fits well in the game.  This is easily a great, if not the sole, reason to buy a Wii.  Only true Metroid fans will have any qualms with this game.  If Nintendo keeps getting games of this caliber(and they will) and the Wii will be here for a long while.

title: Not for 4k gaming. Downgrade to reach 4k resolution is nauseating
text:
This isn't the console to buy if you're interested in playing in 4k. As of October 2017, I would not recommend buying this console unless you're only going to play video games in 1080p. I bought the Xbox One S about 2 weeks ago to hold me over until the Xbox One X comes out. Yes, I know I was only going to own it for a month but whatever, it's already been returned and I'll just keep my original X1 and not play in 4k.

Having owned Xbox 360 (x2), Xbox One, Xbox One S, PS4, PS4 Pro, and a gaming PC, I can say that it's not gonna cut it for 4k. What put me over the edge is the new Shadow of War game. When plugged into my 4k display, the game looked grainy, fuzzy, had no textures and overall made me nauseous just playing it. I also noticed the same thing with Battlefield 1. I knew it couldn't be the display since everything looks great on my PS4 Pro and when outputting 4k on my PC. Thought maybe it was the game but after downloading Shadow of War on PC, the difference was clear. Even in 1080p on PC, the game just looks 100x better. Textures, shadows, lighting, cutscenes, everything was so much sharper. I was originally questioning Shadow of War since I read such good things about the visuals but after playing on PC, I won't even bother going back to my Xbox version until the X1X comes out.

I knew that it wasn't the game and that the Xbox One S just couldn't handle it. Even back on a 1080p tv the game was less than stellar and obviously developers are pushing out content better than what the original hardware can handle. This is truly a shame since many people who own this console will install a new game expecting the latest graphics and be thoroughly disappointed. Had I not been able to return it, I would have sold it immediately for whatever I could get.

Aside from hardly "upscaling" to 4k, the console is great. Smaller and quieter than the original Xbox One. It's got a really nice design and it felt faster just browsing menus and navigating the dashboard. Unfortunately, I have about 85 games on my HDD so playing games is what I do. I knew the S wasn't really an "upgrade" but it was definitely disappointing to see a console that advertised upscaling and HDR capability to look so awful. Many say you won't notice a performance increase with the S but I immediately noticed a performance DECREASE.

If you want to play games on a 4k display, I would definitely recommend the Xbox One X or the PS4 Pro. However, for the money and the fact that a new Playstation isn't coming until 2019 at the absolute earliest, I'd suggest a Xbox One X.

Hope this review helps. I was really excited about this console and wanted to love it but after seeing what it can do with the latest games, it's clear it's not meant for 4k.

title: Affordable SSD that works well as an OS drive
text:
What can a 256gb drive be used for? If one wishes to have storage space, we're talking in Terabytes, not Giga. For portable storage, a micro-sd card or usb pen drive has just as much storage for about the same price. So what niche does a 256gb, M.2 drive fit in?

There are two possibilities that I can think of:
1. A live-usb linux distro install. When combined with a USB 3.1 enclosure, this drive can be used to boot a PC into a linux operating system without affecting the internal drive of the computer. This can be useful for troubleshooting or simply testing out various distros. A drive like this would perform much better than a micro-sd or usb-pen drive.
2. Used as an internal OS drive for a computer. Even with Windows' requirements for space, a 256GB NVME drive will perform better than a traditional Sata drive, meaning faster boot up and faster app launching. It is always good practice to keep your data and OS separate, so for your pictures, videos, and other large files, put them on a separate drive, but use this drive to install your operating system on. This gives you the freedom to refresh your system without fear of losing data.

Specific to this Pioneer 256GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Gen 3x4 Internal Solid State Drive, I currently have it in an external enclosure and am testing Windows 11 (which is only in Insider Preview at the time of this writing). I ran a crystal disk mark against it and posted the picture. I'm happy with this drive and how well Windows runs on it, even through USB.

I baked these in a 350 degree Fahrenheit oven for 18-22 minutes and then left them inside the oven (with the oven off) to dry for a full 60 minutes as per the instructions. To me this was a pain to do. They came out terrible looking due to not having a smaller cutter (see photo).

The mix ingredients are whole wheat flour, sorghum flour, flaxseed, carrots, beef bone broth, parsley, monocalcium phosphate, sodium bicarbonate, and corn starch.

For the current price of $9.99 plus the cost of a farm fresh egg and some oil and water, I got 4 teapots, 8 odd shapes, and 4 tiny teapot holes out of this (see photo). This is entirely too much work. I am glad dogs do not eat with their eyes because what I produced looked terrible to me.

title: 4 watt heating pad w/ fleece sleeve, double decker cube, bed w/ scratcher above, catnip included
text:
This review is for the "Playhouse" option.

We love K&H products. We have been especially keen on using their heating pads for several years now. Between our aging kitties, and even our well "insulated" *cough-fat-cough* tabby, they have all enjoyed luxuriating on a heating pad during the coldest days of winter. We don't keep a real warm house, so cozy spots are a must.

The heating pads are great. The level of heat is akin to the warmth left behind when someone has been sitting in a spot for awhile. They aren't the kind that get hot, which is good. They are very low wattage (4 watts) and produce a "barely there" level of warmth to the touch, but it is enough to allow a cat or dog to get warm, stay warm and not have to rely on their own body heat. If you have an aging or ill pet, know that this will help so much. They likely won't get over heated, but please make sure they can get away as needed. Not comfortable or safe to be too hot either. While it is instructed to be turned on and off when not in use, I have kept all of mine running 24/7 for a few months at a time. No issues, but that is up to you. Check out reviews for just their heating pads and see that it is mentioned by customers. For what it is worth, I am only comfortable buying heating pads from K&H, and would only do that with their products. I've just relied on this brand for so long, I guess I have built in trust? Hopefully it continues.

We also happen to love this style of cube bed. Well, my smaller cats do. Has always been hit and miss for my larger cats.
--These cube styles are amazingly sturdy (we have different brands, styles, and they all hold up). They come folded, just add insert to make base sturdy, then the "lid" which serves to further stabilize it but also creates a second tier. Here it is used as a scratching post, play area.
--The opening on this is smaller than some, so it will depend on your cat whether they will enjoy this or not.
--The interior pad is a zippered sleeve for the heating unit.
--There is a slit in the back of the cube to allow the cord to trail through for plugging in.
--The black fluffy sleeve is fleecy and soft.

This is the first I have seen a double decker with scratching pad in it. Know that it could be left out and simply use that space as a top bunk for sleeping. Just as a cozy blanket or other bedding. The scratcher has a solid bottom so it could just sit on the floor. It is well constructed pad. Also includes two little packets of cat nip. Cute!

The weather is just turning here in NY, so I will getting out my other K&H heating pads as well as looking for the best place for this. I am already thinking it will be most utilized by my ancient boy, Joey who is 18 years old and will likely want easy access to a heat source. He has a little arthritis so his comfort is paramount.

As awesome as the cube style beds are, the aren't huge. My only (mild) let down is that this is smaller than my other cube style beds. Not a huge difference (a little shorter, and a few inches less deep). For example, one of mine is 15"x 15"x 17" and this is, 12" x 14" x 15". It is perfect for my smaller cats (less than 10 lbs) but not sure my bigger tabby would try to sleep in in. Take note of the size of the sleeping area to determine if this is right for your kitties/small dog. I see that there is a bench style "duplex" also offered (longer, has two openings, optional divider insert, heating pad, and top tier is a padded lid). So just see what looks best. Love the other option too.

Packaging: small square easy open box with just this folded cube and supplies, as well as instruction leaflet. Box is a typical full color, glossy, box that you would find as if it were sold on store shelf. Excellent for gift. Of course, packed in a brown box for shipping.

Overall pleased. If we could do half ratings, I would go with 4.5 stars. I am pleased enough to go with 5, as I think it is a very good addition to our home, and I am pretty sure my old boy will be making use of this as the temps drop. The attention to detail is what I expect from K&H, and they do not disappoint. So 5 it is.

Take care :)

The mouse requires one AA battery (included). To change the battery, just lift off the top of the mouse. The keyboard requires two AA batteries (included). To change the keyboard batteries, you push up the strip across the top (the part with “Logi” on it). title: Crystal Clear Film, Easy to Apply, No Loss of Sensitivity
text:
This crystal-clear screen protector film is very easy to apply. It's pre-cut to exactly fit the Kindle Fire touch screen, and it presses on without any need for additional adhesive. After the film is applied, there is no loss of sensitivity in the touch screen.

The application process is very simple: (1) clean the screen thoroughly, using the included microfiber cloth; (2) use the #1 tab to remove the plastic stiffener/shield from one side of the double-sided film; (3) position the uncovered side of the film on the Kindle Fire screen (holding the film by the #2 tab, starting at one corner, and allowing the film to fall gently onto the screen); (4) use the included smoothing card to get rid of bubbles; (5) use the #2 tab to remove the remaining plastic stiffener/shield; and (6) use the smoothing card again to get rid of any bubbles. The whole process took me less than 10 minutes.

Whenever I apply screen protector film, I usually have to try two or three times to get everything right. With this kit, the first application was successful, because the film adhered properly at the edges, and all but one tiny bubble smoothed out. Now, should I ever need to re-apply the film, I have the second shield in reserve.

It's probably worth noting that the Kindle Fire has a larger screen than an iPhone or iPod Touch or camera viewfinder, so that the risk of getting dust particles under the film during application to the Fire is higher. Also, it may not be necessary to install protective film on the Fire at all, because the touch screen is supposed to be made of particularly tough, scratch-resistant glass.

title: Decent port of the 3DS classic
text:
Yes i said "classic" for a 3DS game...because this probably (aside from the obvious Mario entries) was the first 3rd party "classic" for the 3DS for me...and is still the optimum system to play it on in my opinion (withOUT a circle pad pro mind you!).

That stated, a lot was kept the same in this PS3 port, and that's both a good and bad thing. Good in that they didn't go ResEvil 6 and change a bunch of sequences to outdated Dragons Lair/God of War button mashing marathons. But bad in that, if you played the 3DS version, there isn't much left here to discover other than the slightly more textural graphics redefined for a bigger screen and...being able to play it on said bigger screen.

In the canon of Resident Evil games, the story gets pretty ridiculous...but that kind of became expected after Resident Evil 5 (and then furthermore after this came out, when ResEvil 6 was released). But the gameplay harkens back to somewhere between Resident Evil 4 and 5. You don't have to worry about toting around an artificial AI (for the most part)...there's a bit of strategy involved with upgrading your weapons, and you do need to shoot accurately and conserve ammo at times. But those looking for a massive amount of puzzles and creepy build of 0, CV, or 4 (let alone 1/2/3), might want to look elsewhere. The "thrills" aren't cheap like the car crashes and car chases of part 6. But the only go AS deep as "you better get some life and some bullets soon before you turn that corner and a hunter smacks you". Oh yeah spoiler alert, Hunters are back, and there's a lot of them at times!

Recommended for the longtime Resident Evil fan who got turned off by parts 5/6/OpRacoon City/whatever other offshoots in the series since 2007. But for those totally new, forget this and start with ResEvil 4...then work your way back...then come to this one. Then do 5 and 6.

title: Good Basic Protection for Your Laptop
text:
I have a sleeve for my tablet that works out very well for me. It provides some protection for the screen and provides some limited protection against drops and bumps. This is the first sleeve I have used for a laptop and so far I like it. It is appreciably cheaper than a laptop bag or backpack, but it also has less room for accessories.

The sleeve I have is the 15.6” version and it fits my laptop almost perfectly. There is a small amount of wiggle room in the sleeve so that the laptop can slide a little from side to side and it’s just enough to make slipping the laptop in and taking it back out much easier. There is sufficient padding around the edges to make this sleeve useful for bumps and bangs but it will not protect the laptop within from hard drops on the edge.

The outer material is a tight woolen weave and it does a good job of repelling water (though it is not completely waterproof). When splashed with water, the majority of the water beads up and rolls off, and of what remains most can be simply brushed off. The end result is a very slightly damp surface, nowhere near enough to get the laptop inside even slightly wet. So, when toting the sleeve outside it will effectively protect the laptop inside from rain.

There are two pockets inside this sleeve. One is lined in a fleece-like soft material that gently cushions the laptop and allows it to slide in and out more easily. The other pocket is zippered and it is lined in vinyl; it is a good place to put papers, smaller accessories like a travel mouse and other small items. I listen to audiobooks to fall asleep at night so I wear "sleep" earbuds as to not disturb my wife. I usually buy the soft silicone type, which never have good audio quality, but does the job. title: Good HDMI-CEC support; unimportant to most, important to me.
text:
I purchased this Panasonic Soundbar in June of 2013. At the time, my requirements were:
- Good sound (can't afford GREAT sound)
- Wireless Subwoofer
- HDMI input and good HDMI-CEC support
- Bluetooth support

In my search, I tested the [[ASIN:B00811NMMI Toshiba SBX4250]] and the [[ASIN:B00BLX9510 Samsung HW-F450]] from my local Costco. My final choice was the Panasonic.

Sound:
- Acceptable sound -- The front speakers are not a big improvement over the built-ins. With the subwoofer turned off, it is easy to mistake the Panasonic sound bar with the speakers from the Television.
- Good subwoofer -- The sub sounds good even at high volumes and fills out the overall sound from the sound bar.
- The Samsung has clearer mid and high ranges so the Panasonic seems slightly muffled in comparison.
- Overall sound better than the Toshiba.
- Wireless range for the subwoofer is short -- especially if placed behind the sofa (interference from people sitting in front of it). Range is about 15 feet with clear line of sight.

Decoders and Passthrough:
- AC3 and DTS Decoder (Toshiba lacks DTS)
- ARC (Audio Return Channel) -- If you use the Netflix app built in to your TV, audio is generated by your TV. Normally, an "optical out" cable from the TV back to the sound bar is necessary. ARC removes that need.

HDMI-CEC (also Aquos Link, Anynet+, Bravia LinkSync, Regza Link, etc):
This is where the Panasonic beats the Samsung. HDMI-CEC allows Televisions to control a connected device -- no matter the brand; The TV remote should be able to turn on a bluray player and send navigation (up/down/etc) and standard playback buttons without the need for a second remote control.

In the case of a sound bar, through HDMI-CEC:
1. The sound bar should turn on when the TV turns on -- Panasonic does this, Samsung does not.
2. The TV should play all sound through the sound bar and volume buttons on the TV remote should control volume on the sound bar -- Panasonic does this.
3. Turning on a bluray player, the sound bar should turn on and switch to the correct input automatically. The TV should also turn on and switch to the correct input -- Panasonic does this. It's then up to your TV do its part.

In conclusion, I chose the Panasonic because it gave me the ability to eliminate a remote control through HDMI-CEC (which Samsung didn't) and it had both AC3 and DTS decoders (which Toshiba didn't). With the added ability to play music from my phone through bluetooth, I'm still happy with my purchase one year later.

Tip: Unlike the Samsung and Toshiba, the Panasonic has a small "receiver" unit that adds another machine to your entertainment center. For me, I use some velcro strips and attach the "receiver" to the back of my TV. It is only 1 ¾" thick which was thinner than my wall mount.

title: A Comic Book in Video Game's Clothing
text:
Disclosure: Played as a PSN download

It seems TellTale has found, and mastered, a niche: Take a comic book (okay, okay...'graphic novel'), and make it interactive by turning it into a video game. While that rarely seems to work when a company tries to do the same with a movie, TellTale has expanded on what they did perfectly with [[ASIN:B007WWW2C8 The Walking Dead]] and given gamers and comic book fans alike another fantastic release with The Wolf Among Us.

The Wolf Among Us is based on Bill Willingham's [[ASIN:140122427X Fables]] comic book series. And unlike The Walking Dead where the characters were mostly different but lived in a parallel time period as the characters in the source material, the characters in The Wolf Among Us are straight out of the source material. I was a huge fan of The Walking Dead comic before I played the TellTale game, but I have not read the Fables comics, so I cannot confirm whether or not the game follows the comic book storyline. My understanding is that it does not, but I'll come back and clarify that once I do indeed confirm.

But like The Walking Dead Game, you certainly don't have to have read the comics to enjoy this game; just be sure that you are planning to get into and be part of a story-rich experience. And here's the gist: Turns out that fairy tale creatures created in writing (or film) actually `come to life', and many of them have taken residence in an area of New York City called...you guessed it... Fabletown. The sheriff, Bigby Wolf, that's right..."Big Bad Wolf," is protector of all the Fabletown characters, and when one of them is murdered, you take on the role of Sheriff Bigby and try to figure out whodunit.

Along the way in just the first episode you'll meet characters from stories such as Little Red Riding Hood, the Three Little Pigs, Snow White, The Wind in the Willows, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, Beauty and the Beast, Beowulf, The Wizard of Oz and a couple of other popular (and not so popular) fairy tales. But these characters are a bit...shall we say...out of character as they curse, party hearty and behave quite differently from that in which the stories that created them. The game earns its M rating.

There are plenty of action sequences, but your time in this game is mostly spent literally being a part of the story making some tough (and some not so tough) decisions. It's the tough decisions that will affect how the rest of the game unfolds for you, and you'll have to live with the consequences of every option you choose.

TellTale has done it again: The Wolf Among Us is excellent...especially for just a point and click. It's a gritty and graphic interactive comic book, and it's very story-rich. The graphics are appropriately very comic-bookesque. And as far as gameplay, I really do feel like I'm a character in a comic book! You might not like this game if shooters or action games are your thing. You will love this game if you read comics and graphic novels as I do. Check this game out, or I'll huff and I'll puff and....

text:
These ARLO Q (no base, wired version) cameras get IP addresses from your home network and have their own MAC addresses, and yet, you can't use common software that you can use to view most other IP cameras.

According to their technical support, that's because these IP & MAC address wielding cameras, aren't IP cameras.

You basically don't interact with the cameras, AT ALL. Cameras call their servers, you setup an account on Netgear's servers, and you view what the camera sees Netgear's servers from a website and configure everything on Netgear's website, not the camera's website or interface.

Because of this back and forth ALL "LIVE" VIDEO IS A GOOD 10 SECONDS LAGGING!!!

My roommate, for example, was standing in front of me, before the live feed showed her walking up to the door, getting her keys, and unlocking the door and coming in. And I have 160kbps uploads with Comcast!

What's worse is the motion detection (attached video). Both from front porch or backyard get some leaf shadow at SOME point of the day. And that sets these cameras off constantly. Set at MINIMUM motion detection sensitivity. So I basically can't use them for Motion Detection at ALL since they have dozens of false alarms every single day. Worse yet? At nights, the headlights from every car passing by, sets off the motion detection. AT MINIMUM setting. On both cameras.

A couple of days before I bought these, I also ordered a FOSCAM R4 from Amazon for half the price of one of these cameras. It has tilt, pan, and four times the resolution. You can talk to the camera. You can configure the camera on it's own site. You can interface to it using common IP camera software, OR you can treat them like these, have them call home to their servers, and do everything there. The option is super nice.

Also the FOSCAM's motion detection does not get set off with all the false positives mentioned above.

Their tech support is your generic out of the country, going through unrelated scripts of steps rather than someone knowledgable.

title: Easy peasy back up!
text:
I read some of the reviews and concerns. Many are saying you need the original power adapter. My testing says that is NOT true. I plugged this cube into two separate charging hubs, not apple brand, and both scenarios worked.

You need a micro SD card (not included). Some of the questions in the Q&A shows that shoppers don't realize this. There is no built in hard drive in this cube, you provide the storage.

Turning off auto-sleep/auto-lock may get you through thousands of pictures in one shot. This is what I mean... I'm no stranger to trying out different back-up programs. The current program we use is from Plex. When the iphone is backing up to my plex server, the iphone doesn't know that plex is working, so it goes to sleep after about 50 pictures. When it goes to sleep, plex stops backing up. So I always turn off auto-sleep prior to backing up. With the Qubii, the iphone KNEW that it was working, so it "almost" never went to sleep. I said almost because after 4000 files, for some reason, the phone went to sleep. Still, this is much, much, better than the plex app. When I started Qubii again, it picked up where it left off and backed the remaining 1000+ files. But I did the test one more time to make sure! I cleared the micro sd card, and I reset the Qubii count. This time I turned off auto-sleep/auto-sleep on the iphone, and it backed-up the entire camera roll of over 5000 photos and videos in one shot! More trials need to be done to conclusively say this thing can't get through 5000 files without the auto-sleep disabled.

After backing up everything, you should remove your SD card from the Qubii and transfer them to a larger permanent hard drive where you store your collection. The next time you charge your phone, the Qubii will remember the photos it already backed-up even if those photos are no longer on the SD card. So you can always clear your SD card. For whatever reason, if you need the Qubii to back-up the same photos again, like I did when I was testing things out, all you have to do is RESET the Qubii count, which you can do in the Back Up Settings in the app.

Below are the two pictures showing you the scenarios in which I tested this Qubii. Both scenarios used third party charging hubs, but I believe I had the original apple cable. As with all products dependent on apps.. one Apple update can ruin everything. LOL! So these types of app products depend on the company to stick around, so that if Apple breaks anything, they can fix it with a new firmware update. Qubii was on Kickstarter, but only time will tell. As is, this is an amazing product.

title: All plastic, no 1080P recording, and read my advice regarding micro sd card insertion...
text:
I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling.

This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.

title: Epic Fantasy RPG
text:
I've been considering getting this game for some time, but I was unsure. I bought it on sale recently, and it turned out to be one of the best games I have ever played. It is definitely worth it even at full price, and you will be hard pressed to find a game that will give you more play time and enjoyment for your money. Without completing anywhere near all of the side quests available, Origins and Origins: Awakening gave me a solid 72 hours of game play. And that is just one character! This game has great replay value, and you can easily milk hundreds of hours from it.
The game play is fantastic, and the world is huge and diverse, with very good voice acting and character writing, amazing stories, and satisfying reactions based on your choices. If you love traditional RPGs, this game is for you. But for a few bugs that are few and far between (and mostly inconsequential), this game is nearly perfect, and even though a couple of years old, it feels fresh and engaging.
The graphics are nothing overly special, but the game is relatively bugless, and feels great. You won't find yourself lamenting your purchase.
The game also has a huge amount of mods available online to customize the game play.
Overall, this is a great game, and in my top ten games of all time. If you are considering buying this, do it! I don't regret it, and neither will you.

title: The North Grove Must Never Be Lost
text:
Disclosure: Played as a PSN download

TellTale is on a roll! Two great seasons of The Walking Dead, then The Wolf Among Us, and now Game of Thrones. Similar to The Walking Dead series where any fan of the comic book was now able to interactively participate and be part of a story that ran parallel to the source material, Game of Thrones allows players to become new cast-members in the story whose timeline is concurrent with the hit show.

In the first episode called Iron From Ice, you start out as Gared Tuttle, a squire to Lord Gregor Forrester who is a loyal Stark Bannerman. Your initiation to the game begins at The Red Wedding, where you know as a fan of the show is not a good place to be as a Stark or someone loyal to the Starks. Right from the get-go you are thrown into a chaotic journey with plenty of action sequences, but your time in this is mostly spent literally being a part of the story making some tough (and some not so tough) decisions. It's the tough decisions that will affect how the rest of the game unfolds for you, and you'll have to live with the consequences of every option you choose.

In Iron From Ice you'll also play as Ethan Forrester, the young heir to House Forrester who is forced to become a man way before his time, and you'll play as Lord Forrester's daughter Mira, a handmaiden for King Joffrey's bride Margaery Tyrell. I'll tell you what: 1) If you never thought you'd be nervous talking to Cersei Lannister, tell me how you feel about having to have spoken with her after playing this game! And 2) The show portrays Ramsey Snow as a demented sadist, and this game will not make Ramsey any more pleasant than the show does.

The game gives you the option of "rewinding" back to a specific checkpoint, and you can go forward from there and choose a different option that overwrites your original decisions if that's your style. But I don't do that. The game gives you four save slots, so I'd prefer a complete reply in a new save slot. I tried to make my character call "the right move" when presented with choice; but there is a time limit when decision time comes, and sometimes you may regret a hasty decision. For example, in just Episode 1 you'll have to choose between making a life and death decision, and by the end of the game I have no idea if I made the "right" choice or if it would have affected how Episode 1 ended for me. The game certainly gets an A for replay value.

Importantly, you certainly don't have to have seen the show (or read the book) to enjoy this game (but it does help). In fact after a playthrough of this game, if you had not been watching the show I'll bet you will be now. This is a great, STORY HEAVY game. If you liked the point & click, comicbook-esque style and graphics of TellTale's previous entries, you will be fine with this. If you are strictly a run and gun gamer looking for nextgen graphics, stay far, far away.

title: Works Better than Expected for the Price; Needs a Heavier Weighted Base
text:
I have a teenage son who likes gaming on the PC and he has been wanting a new microphone for a while since his headset failed. I was given the opportunity to check this one out, and so far it has worked well. I do have complaint with it, though it’s not a deal breaker.

This is a USB-based microphone so it does not take up the audio jack when plugged in. This is good as it does not preempt a standard headphone set when it’s plugged in. Windows 10 detects it and it is immediately available as an audio input device. No special set-up and no driver downloads are required – it’s plug and play.

In use the sound quality has been good considering the price. In a two-way chat, those who have been on the other end of the discussion have told us that they can hear what is being said more clearly and there is less static than the previous microphone we were using, one that was quite a bit more expensive but still not high-end. That’s really all we could ask.

The one issue I have with it is that the base is not weighted well at all and it is very easy to tip it over or knock the microphone from where it sits on the desk. It’s easy enough to fix by either attaching it to a heavier base, using double-sided tape or even Velcro to secure it to the desk, or some other rigging to anchor the microphone assembly to the workspace. In the grand scheme of things, this is a minor issue; that said, I would rather spend slightly more and have a weighted base that isn’t as easily toppled.

For the price this is a good microphone that works better than could be reasonably expected. There is some room for improvement that would increase the cost slightly, but it would make the difference between being a good product and being a great one.

title: Just OK for the Keyboard
text:
I try real hard to be honest in every review. Some vendors take offense to honesty and products that are not a 5-star rating. But, we on Amazon, truly depend on each other and honesty for products that we want to purchase. We are all different but for me this is my honest assessment. The tablet case does secure the LG G f8 (8inch) tablet well. But, I have had a similar case in the past for my Kindle Fire and never had any issues. It is very strong and durable. My issue is with the keyboard and how it secures with the tablet case. The keyboard is a sturdy construction and not a silicone keypad. BUT, there is not tiny mouse pad within its design. That means to make my LG G tablet truly functional for writing documents, emails and the such I need to have an additional item - a wireless mouse; otherwise why need a keyboard. So, I had to order a mini mouse as well which doesn't exactly fit anyplace but in my pocket or carry bag. The other issue is the way the tablet, case and keyboard are designed to be closed. The case elastic strap is actually the same as the one on my kindle Fire and slips around the secured tablet and does it well. However, add a keyboard, which was NOT a design to this tablet holder and you have to decide if you want the keyboard face against your tablet, tight, as that elastic strap secures them both. that means the keyboard is actually not secure by the case but ONLY by the outer elastic strap. Or, you flip the keyboard so that the back of that keypad rests against your tablet screen and it is still only secured by the outer elastic strap. Both methods require that you ensure you keep this tablet case upright so that the keyboard does not slip out of this elastic band as time and use deteriorate the elastic and its tension. So, in essence, this is a case that has been around and works well for Kindle Fire and probably this tablet. but, this case was NOT designed to include a keyboard. this was a vendor added item with an existing product. When you pay $200 for a tablet you want to ensure you do not scratch the screen or damage the tablet. And if you like the use of a keyboard, note that a mouse will also be required and that it may be best to look for alternative cases to accommodate your needs in one neat package
Update: July 2016: well after very limited use the key board is no loner functioning. It's not the charge it is a dead key board. I am a senior and disabled Vietnam veteran appreciate each dollar of my disability pay and do not have that luxury of repeat purchases. So, even though I am only one customer I would consider other products that have a higher reliability and that are not tied to a protective case purchase.

title: They Look Better Than They Sound
text:
I have had several pairs of Panasonic headphones and I regard them as a budget-grade phone that is better than generic but leaves room for improvement. I was hopeful that these phones would be better and would distinguish themselves as better than average. Unfortunately they do not and they suffer from the same issues I have had with other Panasonic phones in the past. They're certainly not bad, but there is some room for improvement.

First off, these look great, though I would stop short of calling them "retro" in appearance. They're styled to be retro-looking, but they betray their youth in the plastic details. That said, they have the cool factor that they are going for and the will stand out over most run-of-the-miss headphones than you'll find most people using.

One of the problems I have with these is strictly a personal preference. When I use over-the-ear phones like these, I want a phone that clamps down tight over my ear and applies some pressure. This does two things for me - it cuts down on the chances that they'll slip off when I look down, and it cuts sound leakage when I am listening to something. These are a more relaxed, loose fit, and this is not to my tastes. There's a good number of users that will be very happy with the way these fit, and as I said this is a preference, so I cannot say this is a fault. It's something to keep in mind, though. Aside from the tightness (or lack thereof), the pads and band are soft and these can be worn for a long while without issue.

These are Bluetooth phones, so I used them to connect to my Android tablet. They connected very quickly and without any real issues. I have no complaints there. They stay connected once paired and the range is good to at least 20-30 feet from the source which is good.

Where these headphones fail, though, is in the most important area - the sound profile. The highs are slightly muddy though not unacceptably so. The bass is present and not overdriven which to me is a very good thing. But, the midrange is not right at all, and as a result the music sounds like it is coming out of a tunnel when I am listening. Yes, I could fix this with an equalizer, but many people will not think to do that or do not have access to one. This is a familiar issue I have had with Panasonic phones, and unfortunately these do not correct the issue.

For speech, these sound just fine.

These are interesting phones and they look good. For those liking a loose fit, they're going to be very comfortable. However, there is an issue in the sound profile that anyone serious about their music will not be able to help but notice, and at the price point it's a more serious issue than if these were inexpensive (budget) headphones.

title: It works, but it isn't the cats' favorite way to get brushed!
text:
We got one of these to see if it would really do any good for grooming our cats.
One cat would let us brush him all day if we could, but our little girl? Well, she
fights every single grooming effort you make, whether it is a toenail trim or a brushing.

We also have a furminator and various wire bristled brushes. I wanted to try this and see
if I could even rub it over our girl cat while she was passing by! Ha!

This does work at getting loose surface hair. It does NOT go down and get the dander-making
coat that most cats have - it stays on the surface. What we found that it also does a nice job on
is after brushing with a bristle-style brush, I go over the kitty with this glove. It pulls all the hair
that was loose on top, as well as hair loosened from the other grooming.

It is reasonably easy to clean, if you "roll" the hair off. If you try to pick at sections, you'll
have a mess.

This also does a good job on furniture, believe it or not. I "brushed" my office chair, which is
a favorite place for our boy cat to lounge. I was able to get a lot of loose hair off the chair
with this glove.

So, is it the cats' favorite way to get brushed? Nope. Neither one cares for it much, even though
the male will tolerate it. Is it my favorite? Nope - it doesn't take off enough hair to be useful.
But, it is still a nice way to spend time with your cat, and many cats will enjoy the extra attention,
no matter what you are using. As long as you are not rough or hard while using this, it seems like it
would be a little massaging and decent for them.
(PS - ours came in red.)

[Ok, I originally gave this product 5 stars, I decided to change my review and give it only 3 after half-year of usage.]

I've owned many Logitech products over the years, one of the many have been Logitech keyboards. The G110 is the fourth Logitech keyboard I've owned, and I have to say it's a really nice looking keyboard, the back lighting is really good for show, but since I don't game in the dark, its nothing that I really I need but overall for aesthetics this keyboard does pretty good. The KB does slide around a bit from time to time, the rubber feet aren't really make it stay put. The keys are also starting to squeak a bit as well, and losing their response.

Overall, this keyboard is decent, but I wouldn't purchase it again if I had the chance to, mainly because the keys, as I've mentioned, and they way the keys are aligned from other keyboards is not for me. For the price ($60+), is asking way too much. Sure the back lighting is nice, but what good is it if the keyboard isn't comfortable. I would only recommend it if it were dropped down by about $45.

title: Terrific outlets, but keep in mind, there are no screws in the middle...
text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* You get two outlet units in this package.
* The outlets are nicely placed so all my little bricks fit. Do not overlook spacing of outlets, they absolutely matter for an efficient design.
* Three 2.4A USB ports.
* One 3.0A USB-C port.
* 1800J surge protection.

THE BAD:
------------
* When I saw the stock photos, I thought the middle dot was the screw location. As it turns out, it's just a led light to show you're protected. So the only downside to this design is that you cannot screw in the unit to the wall. I have several Belkin outlets similar to this and they placed the led lights at a different location, so that the middle is dedicated for a long machine screw. We installed this Addtam unit under an entryway table. We store things under this desk, so we'll have to be careful. Also, without the machine screw securing the outlet in place, when you unplug individual plugs or adapters, you'll need to be careful you don't pull the entire unit out the wall. That could happen with tight fighting plugs. So one hand should hold the unit in place, while the other hand unplugs.

I'll go 4-Stars. It would be 5 if they didn't omit the screw slot.
